title: Training order over structures matters: learning high-agreement anatomy before ambiguous anatomy transfers a stable boundary policy and improves the ambiguous structures.
core_hypothesis: Networks trained first on structures with consistent labels develop boundary-decision policies that transfer as useful priors to ambiguous structures, whereas simultaneous training lets ambiguous-label gradients corrupt the shared boundary representation, so agreement-ordered curricula outperform uniform mixing specifically on low-agreement structures.

title: Minority-structure underperformance in joint multi-organ training is a directional gradient-interference problem, and measuring per-structure gradient geometry predicts which structures suffer.
core_hypothesis: Per-structure gradients conflict directionally in shared layers: some structure pairs exhibit persistent negative gradient cosine, and it is these conflicts, not magnitude imbalance, that predict minority-structure degradation, so conflict-aware update surgery outperforms any reweighting scheme.

title: Same-patient patches within a batch let normalization statistics encode patient identity, inflating validation scores and understating deployment error.
core_hypothesis: When batches mix patches from few patients, normalization statistics become patient-conditional features, models exploit them, and reported validation performance (computed under similar batching) exceeds true per-patient deployment performance, with the gap largest for small-batch 3D pipelines.

title: Binary smoke masks are annotator-threshold artifacts: models trained on them learn the annotator's opacity threshold, not smoke.
core_hypothesis: A segmentation model trained on one annotator's smoke masks internalizes that annotator's implicit transmittance threshold as a global scalar, and most cross-annotator disagreement in model evaluation is explained by this single latent threshold rather than by shape or localization error.

title: Transparent-object segmentation conflates occupancy ('where the glass is') with photometric effect ('where the glass changes the image'), and model errors concentrate where the two diverge.
core_hypothesis: Segmentation errors on transparent objects are not spatially random: they concentrate in the 'occupied but photometrically silent' set (flat clean glass over flat background), and this set can be predicted in advance from a simple local background-modulation score without running the model.

title: Alpha matting, not binary segmentation, is the correct output space for smoke; binary training actively destroys usable density information.
core_hypothesis: Networks trained with binary smoke masks still compute an internal soft-density estimate in intermediate features, and the binarizing head is where the information is lost; a matting-style head on the same backbone recovers density ordering without any density supervision.

title: Visible flame boundaries are exposure artifacts: the same fire produces different 'ground truth' masks depending on camera exposure, making fire GT a function of the sensor, not the scene.
core_hypothesis: The area of the human-annotated flame mask for a fixed physical fire varies systematically and substantially with exposure settings, and models trained on mixed-exposure data learn an average that is wrong for every specific exposure.

title: 2D smoke masks are geometrically inconsistent across simultaneous viewpoints, proving the 2D task is a projection of an ill-posed problem models silently resolve with view-specific heuristics.
core_hypothesis: Multi-view captures of the same plume, annotated independently per view, will produce masks that cannot be explained by any single 3D density threshold; the inconsistency magnitude grows with plume thinness and background contrast difference between views.

title: Per-pixel classification is a category error for mixed pixels: cross-entropy training on media provably biases boundaries toward hard edges, and the bias is measurable as gradient sharpening.
core_hypothesis: Cross-entropy-trained media segmenters exhibit output transition widths (logit gradient at boundaries) that are systematically narrower than the true alpha transition width, and this sharpening bias grows with training time; regression to alpha removes it.

title: Transparent objects should be segmented by detecting background distortion, not object appearance: an explicit background-reconstruction branch is the load-bearing component.
core_hypothesis: The information a network uses to find glass is predominantly 'this region disagrees with the expected background continuation'; making that explicit (predict the background, segment where reconstruction residual is structured) generalizes to unseen glass shapes and categories better than direct mask prediction at equal capacity.

title: Smoke, fire, fog, and dust need a third annotation ontology category ('media') distinct from stuff and things, and annotator agreement will jump when it exists.
core_hypothesis: A large share of inter-annotator disagreement on smoke/fire in panoptic-style annotation is caused by the ontology (thing-vs-stuff forced choice), not by perceptual difficulty, and introducing an explicit 'media' category with its own rules (no instance identity, soft extent allowed) measurably increases agreement at fixed annotation time.

title: Smoke boundaries are near-fractal, so boundary-based metrics do not converge as resolution increases; every boundary F-score for smoke is resolution-relative.
core_hypothesis: The measured boundary length of high-effort smoke masks grows as a power law with image resolution (box-counting dimension noticeably above 1) over the practical resolution range, whereas solid-object masks plateau; consequently boundary-tolerance metrics change model rankings when evaluation resolution changes.

title: Inter-annotator disagreement maps on smoke are a free density sensor: disagreement rate is a monotone function of optical thickness.
core_hypothesis: Pixelwise annotator disagreement probability on smoke is a monotone (roughly sigmoidal) function of true transmittance, so a model trained to predict the disagreement map recovers relative optical depth ordering without any density supervision.

title: Video-annotated smoke labels contain motion information that single-frame models cannot access, creating a hidden irreducible error floor in frame-level benchmarks.
core_hypothesis: A quantifiable fraction of smoke pixels in video-annotated datasets are statically ambiguous (indistinguishable from haze/walls/clouds in the single frame) and were resolved by the annotator using motion; single-frame model errors concentrate on exactly this subset, forming a floor no single-frame architecture can cross.

title: Trimap-style 'certain core + uncertain halo' smoke annotation dominates precise-boundary annotation in information per annotator-minute.
core_hypothesis: For fixed annotation time, labeling smoke as (confident-smoke core, confident-background, unlabeled halo) yields models at least as good as precise-boundary labels on region metrics, and better calibrated in the halo band, because the halo honestly encodes ambiguity instead of a fabricated boundary.

title: Smoke masks are systematically truncated in the downwind/diffusion direction, and models inherit a directional under-segmentation bias aligned with flow.
core_hypothesis: The signed boundary error of human smoke masks (vs physically defined extent in controlled scenes) is largest and negative at the downstream end of plumes, and trained models reproduce this anisotropy: their misses concentrate downwind even on symmetric test plumes.

title: Majority-vote consensus masks are worse training targets than single-annotator masks for media, because vote-averaging fabricates a boundary no physical threshold produces.
core_hypothesis: Models trained on per-annotator masks (randomly sampling one annotator per image, preserving internal consistency) outperform models trained on majority-vote masks of the same annotation pool, on both physically defined test labels and per-annotator test labels.

title: Positives-only smoke annotation ignores 'proof of absence' evidence (crisp background visibility), inducing an over-segmentation bias in clutter that negative-evidence labels would fix.
core_hypothesis: Because unmarked regions mix 'no smoke' with 'unsure', models treat low-texture unmarked regions as weakly positive, producing false positives on clean but hazy-looking areas; adding sparse explicit negative-evidence annotations (regions certified smoke-free by visible sharp detail) reduces false positives more per label than adding equal-cost positive labels.

title: Single-image smoke decomposition via a two-parameter Beer-Lambert model per pixel is identifiable under a low-frequency background prior, giving physics-grounded pseudo-labels for free.
core_hypothesis: Under a locally low-frequency background assumption, per-pixel transmittance is approximately identifiable from a single frame for mid-density smoke, and a solver based on this yields transmittance maps accurate enough to supervise a network that then beats mask-trained baselines on density-sensitive tasks.

title: There is a computable per-pixel detectability limit for thin smoke (contrast vs noise), and model errors saturate this limit rather than reflecting model quality.
core_hypothesis: A physics-derived detectability index (local smoke-induced contrast change divided by local noise estimate) predicts per-pixel miss probability nearly deterministically across different architectures, implying current models are already at the information limit for thin smoke and remaining differences are elsewhere.

title: Fire is an emitter, not a surface: a measurable share of 'fire segmentation error' is actually the model segmenting illumination cast by fire onto smoke and walls.
core_hypothesis: A large, quantifiable fraction of false-positive fire pixels in current models lies in fire-illuminated (but not burning) regions, and this fraction grows as ambient light decreases, because the emitter/illuminated distinction requires dynamic-range headroom that dark scenes remove.

title: The refractive background-warp field, not appearance, is the strongest single cue for glass: predicting warp magnitude localizes glass better than direct mask regression at low data.
core_hypothesis: A model trained to predict the dense background-displacement field (supervisable in controlled or synthetic scenes) and thresholding its magnitude will localize refractive objects with better sample efficiency and better shape generalization than an equal-capacity direct mask model, because the warp cue is category-agnostic.

title: Glass segmentation accuracy is secretly a function of camera viewpoint via specular highlight geometry, so datasets with photographer-height bias produce models with angle-dependent blind spots.
core_hypothesis: Model performance on the same physical glass objects varies systematically with camera elevation and azimuth (not just scale), tracking the visibility of speculars from the training viewpoint distribution; robot-height and ceiling-camera viewpoints suffer predictable drops.

title: Smoke is chromatically near-neutral by scattering physics; a chromaticity-invariance test separates smoke from white solid distractors, and current models fail it.
core_hypothesis: True smoke overlays preserve a recoverable trace of background chromaticity (hue direction persists at reduced saturation), while opaque white/gray distractors do not; a simple chromatic-consistency statistic separates the two cases, and current models' false positives on white objects are concentrated where this statistic says 'opaque'.

title: Two orthogonal polarization captures may make transparent-object segmentation nearly trivial, implying the field's difficulty is an RGB-sensor artifact rather than an algorithmic frontier.
core_hypothesis: The degree-of-polarization image separates glass surfaces from background so cleanly in common indoor/outdoor conditions that a shallow classifier on two-polarization input approaches the accuracy of large RGB models, revealing that most published difficulty is sensor-induced.

title: Cast shadows of smoke are often more detectable than the smoke itself, and current models make no use of this indirect evidence.
core_hypothesis: In sunlit scenes there exists a measurable regime where smoke-shadow contrast exceeds direct smoke contrast, and current segmenters' predictions are causally independent of shadow evidence (masking the shadow region does not change the smoke prediction), demonstrating an unexploited information channel.

title: Beyond a computable distance, smoke and atmospheric haze are physically indistinguishable in a single image, so distant-smoke labels supervise context recognition, not medium recognition.
core_hypothesis: There is a distance/optical-depth regime where no single-image statistic separates smoke from haze (their transfer functions coincide); labels in this regime force models to rely on geographic/contextual priors (plume shape, source landmarks), which is why distant-smoke detectors transfer poorly across regions.

title: Motion evidence has opposite spatial structure for smoke (dense interior texture motion) vs glass (sparse edge/specular motion), suggesting a motion-sparsity router as a unified media-segmentation front end.
core_hypothesis: The spatial sparsity of temporal change is a two-sided signature: volumetric media produce spatially dense, temporally decorrelating change across their support; refractive solids produce sparse, edge-concentrated, geometrically consistent change; a router computing motion-sparsity statistics can dispatch pixels to the correct downstream model and beat both single-task models on mixed scenes.
mutation_note: MUTATE. A router dispatching pixels to existing pretrained specialists is Module-A+B assembly. Salvage: the two-sided physical signature (dense decorrelating temporal change for volumetric media vs sparse edge-locked geometric change for refractive solids) is a falsifiable observation claim - validate the statistic's bimodality and cross-domain stability first; the router is at most a downstream application.

title: Point prompts 'fall through' translucent media at a rate that tracks opacity: prompt fall-through of a frozen promptable segmenter is a zero-training opacity probe.
core_hypothesis: The probability that a point prompt inside a medium returns a background-object mask (fall-through rate) is a monotone function of local medium opacity, making the frozen model an unintentional opacity sensor whose output can supervise or calibrate dedicated media models.

title: Different foundation models disagree about glass in characteristic ways (depth sees through it, segmenters segment behind it), and their disagreement map is itself a free glass detector.
core_hypothesis: Pixels on transparent surfaces produce a distinctive cross-model inconsistency signature (e.g. monocular depth reporting the far surface while stereo or shading cues report near; segmenters labeling the occluded object), and thresholding a cross-model inconsistency score localizes glass with accuracy competitive with weakly supervised dedicated detectors, using zero glass-specific training.

title: Open-vocabulary segmenters respond to smoke's context, not smoke: text-driven 'smoke' masks are driven by chimneys, flames, and sky composition rather than the medium's pixels.
core_hypothesis: Open-vocabulary segmentation for media terms is dominated by contextual anchors: pasting real smoke into atypical contexts (indoor office, snowfield) sharply reduces recall, while context-without-medium images (chimney with no smoke, extinguished fire scene) produce confident false masks whose spatial layout tracks where smoke 'should' be.

title: Mask decoders carry a simply-connected topology prior: predicted smoke masks have systematically lower genus (fewer holes, fewer wisp components) than ground truth, and the deficit is architecture-attributable.
core_hypothesis: The topological complexity (component count, hole count) of predicted media masks is bounded well below ground-truth complexity across current architectures, the bound tightens with decoder upsampling aggressiveness, and matching region metrics can coexist with severe topology loss, hiding the defect from standard evaluation.

title: Prompt-jitter output variance of a frozen promptable segmenter is a zero-training ambiguity meter that flags boundary-undefined objects before any task model runs.
core_hypothesis: The variance of masks returned by a frozen promptable segmenter under small prompt perturbations is systematically higher over ambiguous media than over solid objects, and an instability map thresholded at a single global value detects 'boundary-undefined object present' with useful accuracy across domains it was never tuned on.

title: Fire segmentation competence is bimodal across illumination (easy at night, hard in daylight), and single aggregate benchmark scores conceal that models fail exactly when visual confirmation matters.
core_hypothesis: Public fire segmenters' per-image accuracy distribution is strongly bimodal with illumination as the latent factor; day-condition accuracy is far lower than the aggregate suggests, and cross-dataset ranking of methods changes when scores are conditioned on illumination, meaning current leaderboards partially rank datasets' day/night mixes rather than models.

title: Appearance-template video trackers have a computable half-life on smoke set by turbulent decorrelation, so tracking failure is a physical timescale, not a model deficiency.
core_hypothesis: The time for a smoke region's appearance to decorrelate below trackers' matching thresholds is a measurable physical quantity (a function of turbulence intensity and viewing scale), and tracker persistence on smoke is predicted by this half-life across models: no appearance-matching tracker exceeds it, while motion-integration methods can.

title: IoU and matting metrics rank smoke models differently as a matter of course, so 'state of the art' in smoke segmentation is metric-relative in a way the field has not acknowledged.
core_hypothesis: Across a pool of public smoke segmenters, rank correlation between IoU-based orderings and soft/matting-based orderings is low enough that several published-style superiority claims would invert, and the divergence concentrates in models differing in boundary behavior rather than region behavior.

title: Human judges prefer physically plausible smoke masks over pixel-accurate ones, so IoU optimization and perceived quality diverge for media in a way they do not for solids.
core_hypothesis: In forced-choice comparisons, human preference between competing smoke masks disagrees with IoU ordering at a substantial rate, and the disagreement is predicted by plausibility features (connectivity to source, smooth density gradients, flow alignment) that IoU ignores.

title: Benchmark scores for smoke segmentation are uncorrelated with false-alarm rates on smoke-like distractors, because positive-heavy collection made distractors statistically invisible to evaluation.
core_hypothesis: Across public models, standard benchmark scores and false-alarm rates on a purpose-built distractor suite are essentially uncorrelated (or weakly anti-correlated, if aggressive models win benchmarks), meaning model selection by benchmark actively fails to select for deployability.

title: Temporal-consistency metrics penalize physically correct behavior on smoke: real plume boundaries change faster than the smoothness these metrics reward.
core_hypothesis: The frame-to-frame mask change rate of true smoke extents (measurable in controlled captures) exceeds the implicit stability preference of common temporal-consistency metrics, so models optimized for those metrics systematically lag real plume evolution, and the lag is detectable as a directional phase delay in growing plumes.

title: Instance-level metrics (AP, panoptic quality) are undefined-in-practice for plumes because plume countability is unstable: the metric variance induced by arbitrary instance conventions exceeds model differences.
core_hypothesis: Re-annotating the same smoke scenes under different defensible instance conventions (split-by-source, split-by-connectivity, single-media-region) changes instance-metric scores of fixed models by more than typical inter-model gaps, demonstrating that instance metrics on media measure convention agreement rather than model quality.

title: Construct validity for smoke segmentation can be tested by correlating mask outputs with independently measured physical quantities, and current models may fail the test their metrics never apply.
core_hypothesis: In controlled scenes where physical smoke quantities are measured (metered fog output, transmissometer readings), the correlation between model mask statistics and physical quantities is low for models with top label-based scores, and the two evaluation axes (label agreement vs physical correlation) identify different best models.

title: Glass segmentation generalization claims are confounded by object-category leakage: models detect cups and windows, not the material, and shape-novel glass exposes it.
core_hypothesis: Public glass segmenters' performance on category-novel transparent objects (irregular glass art, laboratory apparatus, unusual industrial parts) drops far more than on held-out instances of familiar categories, and a category classifier trained on their intermediate features achieves high accuracy, together demonstrating that current 'material' models are substantially category models.

title: The temporal power spectrum of pixel intensities inside smoke follows a characteristic turbulence-cascade slope that distinguishes it from vegetation motion, water, and flags, providing a physics-anchored feature no dataset shift can remove.
core_hypothesis: Intensity time series within smoke regions exhibit spectral slopes in a characteristic band (inherited from turbulent advection of density fluctuations) that are measurably distinct from the spectra of oscillatory distractors (vegetation: peaked; water: different slope; flags: harmonic), and the slope feature transfers across cameras and scenes with minimal recalibration.

title: Optical-flow divergence is signed by plume physics: young expanding smoke shows positive flow divergence usable as a free weak label distinguishing emission sources from drifting media.
core_hypothesis: The divergence field of optical flow within smoke regions is systematically positive near active sources (volumetric expansion projected to the image) and near zero in passively advected smoke, providing an unsupervised active-source indicator with predictable failure under strong wind shear.

title: Reported flame-flicker frequency cues are partly camera artifacts: flicker features measured through rolling shutter, auto-gain, and compression do not survive sensor swaps, undermining a classical fire-detection assumption.
core_hypothesis: A substantial part of the flicker signal exploited by classical and learned fire detectors is generated or reshaped by the camera pipeline; the same physical fires filmed simultaneously by different sensor/codec chains will yield flicker statistics different enough to flip detector decisions, revealing sensor overfitting where physics was assumed.

title: Gravity-alignment of motion separates the white-media family: smoke rises or drifts, steam rises then vanishes, water spray falls; a reference-direction prior distinguishes classes appearance cannot.
core_hypothesis: The distribution of vertical motion components (relative to a gravity direction available from image or metadata) differs diagnostically between buoyant media (smoke, steam: net upward near source), ballistic media (spray: net downward), and neutral media (dust: wind-locked), enabling a class disambiguation that improves false-alarm rates without any appearance retraining.

title: Temporal frame averaging has opposite effects on smoke visibility depending on background dynamics, and the crossover is computable, enabling an adaptive pre-filter that beats any fixed temporal window.
core_hypothesis: Averaging N frames increases smoke detectability against dynamic backgrounds (noise suppression wins) but decreases it against static backgrounds when smoke itself moves (contrast dilution wins); the optimal N per region is predictable from local background temporal variance and smoke drift rate, and an adaptive-N front end improves any downstream detector.

title: Deliberate camera micro-motion converts glass segmentation from an appearance problem into a geometry problem: induced parallax makes refractive distortion time-varying and thus directly observable.
core_hypothesis: Sub-centimeter camera translations create background-motion anomalies at refractive surfaces (displacement fields inconsistent with any rigid scene interpretation) that are far easier to detect than static appearance cues, so active micro-motion plus a rigidity-violation test outperforms static state-of-the-art on the same scenes at a fraction of model size.

title: Propagated smoke labels in video expire on a measurable timescale (label half-life), and dataset quality is bounded by the ratio of annotation refresh interval to that half-life.
core_hypothesis: The IoU between a propagated smoke mask and the true extent decays approximately exponentially with time offset at a rate set by turbulence and flow speed; datasets whose keyframe interval exceeds the derived half-life contain a predictable fraction of stale labels, and model errors on those datasets concentrate at large offsets from keyframes.

title: Pixelwise thermal-visible disagreement is nearly a direct glass label (opaque in long-wave infrared, transparent in visible), reducing glass detection to cheap cross-modal comparison.
core_hypothesis: A simple disagreement functional between co-registered thermal and visible views (edges present in one and absent in the other, depth-of-content mismatch) localizes glass surfaces with accuracy competitive with supervised visible-only models, while requiring no glass annotations, and its residual errors are complementary to visible-model errors.

title: The assumed thermal advantage for smoke segmentation may be a fire-proximity artifact: for cool or aged smoke, thermal contributes little, and reported fusion gains may vanish.
core_hypothesis: Fusion gains for smoke segmentation are concentrated in scenes where hot sources or heated gases are present in-frame; for ambient-temperature smoke the thermal channel carries near-zero incremental information, and models trained with fusion degrade on cool smoke relative to visible-only models because they learned to rely on heat.

title: A two-band visible/near-infrared contrast ratio estimates scattering particle size, physically separating fine smoke from coarse fog and dust where RGB texture models fail.
core_hypothesis: The ratio of local contrast attenuation between a visible band and a near-infrared band is a monotone proxy for scattering particle size in the relevant regimes, so a two-band sensor with a per-region ratio feature separates fine combustion smoke from coarse water fog and mineral dust with accuracy unreachable by single-band texture analysis.

title: Depth-sensor dropout patterns are material signatures: glass, mirrors, and smoke corrupt active depth in distinguishable ways, providing free training labels from any RGB-D stream.
core_hypothesis: The joint statistics of depth invalidity, depth-behind-surface readings, and intensity dropouts form clusster-separable signatures for glass (far-surface or specular dropout), mirrors (geometry-inconsistent phantom depth), and dense smoke (range-dependent attenuation), so an unsupervised clustering of failure patterns yields material pseudo-labels that can bootstrap segmentation training with zero human annotation.

title: Audio crackle can weakly supervise flame segmentation via sound-source localization, but the load-bearing question is whether audio localization is spatially sharp enough to teach pixels anything.
core_hypothesis: Audio-visual correspondence learning on fire videos yields spatial supervision at a characterizable (coarse) resolution, and this coarse supervision is sufficient to train flame localization to within a bounded factor of pixel-supervised models, because flame appearance is locally distinctive once a rough region is pinned.

title: Flash/no-flash differencing is a near-direct nighttime smoke densitometer: backscatter from the flash illuminates near-camera media while barely changing the background.
core_hypothesis: The difference image between flash and no-flash frames is approximately proportional to near-field scattering density along each ray (given background distance), so thresholding or regressing on flash differentials yields nighttime smoke masks and relative density maps with quality unreachable by passive night imaging, degrading predictably with smoke-to-camera distance.

title: Rolling-shutter row-phase artifacts encode flame temporal dynamics within single frames, turning a sensor defect into a static-image flame-vs-flame-colored-object discriminator.
core_hypothesis: Flames imaged by rolling-shutter sensors exhibit row-wise intensity phase patterns (horizontal banding statistics) reflecting their rapid luminance dynamics, absent in static flame-colored objects (sunsets, orange fabrics, lamps), and a row-spectrum feature detects this within single frames at useful accuracy.

title: Fire segmenters are largely saturated-warm-color detectors: a color-reliance index computed via hue-rotation counterfactuals predicts their false positives and their grayscale collapse.
core_hypothesis: Public fire segmenters' outputs are dominated by a low-dimensional color subspace: hue-rotating fire regions toward blue suppresses detection almost entirely, hue-rotating distractors toward orange induces confident false masks, and a scalar color-reliance index derived from these counterfactuals predicts each model's real-world false-positive rate on sunsets, foliage, and clothing.

title: Smoke segmenters are partly skyline detectors: performance collapses for smoke below the horizon line because datasets overwhelmingly show plumes against sky.
core_hypothesis: Model recall for physically identical smoke is substantially lower when the plume is imaged against terrain backgrounds than against sky, beyond what background contrast differences explain, because models learned 'gray mass touching skyline' as a proxy; drone-view (top-down) smoke suffers most.

title: Tight-cropping collapses smoke recognition far more than solid-object recognition, revealing that models possess almost no intrinsic appearance model of the medium itself.
core_hypothesis: Removing context by tight cropping (or context scrambling) degrades smoke segmentation accuracy by a much larger fraction than it degrades solid-object segmentation, demonstrating that current models encode 'scenes where smoke happens' rather than 'what smoke looks like', with implications for their behavior in novel scene types.

title: Video compression destroys smoke evidence before it destroys solid-object evidence: deployed CCTV bitrates may sit past a cliff where smoke segmentation has silently collapsed.
core_hypothesis: Segmentation accuracy versus bitrate curves are qualitatively different for smoke (steep collapse below a threshold bitrate, driven by gradient quantization and temporal smoothing) than for solid objects (graceful degradation), and common surveillance encoder settings fall below the smoke cliff.

title: Fire context primes smoke hallucination: models exposed to any fire-colored region label nearby fog and haze as smoke, a contextual induction effect measurable with composite scenes.
core_hypothesis: The presence of fire-typical evidence anywhere in the frame raises smoke false-positive rates on unrelated fog/haze regions multiplicatively (not additively), because models learned a scene-level joint prior rather than independent per-region evidence integration; the coupling strength can be measured by factorial composites.

title: Transparent-object models are rim detectors: inpainting the frame/rim of glassware collapses segmentation, exposing that the interior 'transparency understanding' is interpolation between detected edges.
core_hypothesis: Removing rim evidence (inpainting rims, imaging rimless vessels, framing glass so edges are out of view) collapses interior segmentation accuracy disproportionately, showing that current models detect boundary artifacts and fill inward, with near-zero reliance on interior refraction or reflection cues.

title: Steam, smoke, clouds, spray, and fog occupy one undifferentiated 'white volumetric stuff' region in current models' feature space, and representational geometry predicts which confusions are fixable by fine-tuning versus structural.
core_hypothesis: Feature-space analysis (probing, representational similarity) of standard backbones will show white-media classes nearly collinear/overlapping relative to solid-class separations; the degree of overlap per class pair predicts fine-tuning sample efficiency for that discrimination, separating 'latent but unread' distinctions from 'never encoded' ones.

title: Night-fire masks largely trace the camera's glare and bloom, not the fire: models segment the sensor's point-spread function, and mask area is predictable from exposure settings alone.
core_hypothesis: For night scenes, a large fraction of predicted fire-mask area lies in bloom/glare regions rather than combustion regions, and mask area scales with exposure and aperture as the optical point-spread model predicts, meaning night-fire benchmark scores substantially measure reproduction of camera artifacts.

title: Detection latency on growing plumes is the hidden casualty of dataset curation: models trained on photogenic developed plumes activate far later on incipient smoke than their benchmark scores imply.
core_hypothesis: On continuous recordings spanning ignition to developed plume, current models' first-detection times cluster long after human observers' detection times, and the lag correlates with the training set's plume-size distribution: the model has learned what curated smoke looks like, which is definitionally not what early smoke looks like.

title: A taxonomy of 'natural adversarials' for media segmentation (birch trunks, waterfalls, sunbeams, dust devils, contrails) can explain the majority of field false positives with a small closed list.
core_hypothesis: Field false positives concentrate heavily on a small enumerable set of physically smoke-like or fire-like natural phenomena, such that a taxonomy of under twenty categories covers the large majority of false-positive volume, making targeted negative curation vastly more efficient than generic data scaling.

title: Predicting log-transmittance (optical depth) instead of masks makes smoke composition additive, enabling extrapolation to densities never seen in training.
core_hypothesis: Training media models to regress log-transmittance makes overlapping smoke linear in the output space (optical depths add along rays), so models trained only on single-plume scenes will predict two-plume overlaps correctly (additivity generalization) and extrapolate beyond the training density range, which alpha- and mask-space models will fail.

title: Predicting a monotone stack of nested iso-density contours turns one arbitrary annotation threshold into a family, making threshold choice explicit and letting one model serve every application's strictness.
core_hypothesis: A model constrained to output nested mask families (monotone level sets) trained on mixed-threshold data disentangles 'where the density gradient lies' from 'where one annotator cut it', producing per-level accuracy on held-out strictness levels it never saw labeled, which single-threshold models cannot do.

title: The correct target for ambiguous boundaries is a boundary distribution, not a boundary: models should be scored by the likelihood they assign to the population of plausible annotations.
core_hypothesis: Modeling the mask as a distribution (a generative model over plausible masks conditioned on the image) and evaluating by held-out multi-annotator likelihood will rank models differently than point-mask metrics, and distribution-trained models will transfer better across annotation protocols because they capture the ambiguity structure rather than one protocol's realization.

title: Decomposing glass into reflection layer, transmission layer, and distortion field makes segmentation a byproduct, and synthetic-only training of the decomposition may transfer better than real-supervised direct masking.
core_hypothesis: A model trained (on synthetic data where all layers are known) to decompose images into reflection, transmission, and refraction-distortion components learns physics-anchored features that transfer to real glass segmentation with less real data than direct mask models need, because the decomposition is domain-general while mask boundaries are dataset-specific.

title: Turbulent internal motion is a monocular depth cue inside plumes: smoke's 3D structure is partially recoverable from single-camera video, making 2D segmentation a projection of a solvable 3D problem.
core_hypothesis: The statistics of feature motion within a smoke region (velocity dispersion, occlusion ordering of transient features) constrain relative depth layering inside the plume well enough that a monocular video model can recover coarse 3D density structure, verifiable against multi-view reconstruction, and 3D-aware training improves 2D segmentation consistency across views for free.

title: Per-pixel transparent-surface counting (0/1/2+ layers) is a learnable output space that fixes the self-overlap failures binary glass masks cannot even express.
core_hypothesis: Reframing glass segmentation as ordinal layer counting is learnable with modest synthetic supervision, transfers to real layered scenes, and as a side effect improves ordinary single-layer mask accuracy because the counting objective forces the model to localize each optical interface rather than a blurred union.

title: Media need two masks, not one: 'physically present' vs 'photometrically evident' extents diverge measurably, and supervising their difference resolves annotation contradictions at the source.
core_hypothesis: In controlled scenes both extents are separately measurable (presence via physical instrumentation or release geometry, evidence via contrast analysis), their difference region is large for thin media, and jointly supervising both masks yields models whose evidence-mask generalizes across backgrounds while presence-mask calibrates abstention, outperforming single-mask training on each objective separately.

title: Amodal completion helps glass but harms smoke: a dissociation experiment that reveals what 'object permanence' means to segmentation models.
core_hypothesis: Adding amodal-completion objectives improves transparent-object segmentation (glass has definite geometry that completion regularizes) while degrading smoke segmentation (completion imposes closed-shape priors on an object with no canonical shape), producing a clean double dissociation that localizes where shape priors help versus hurt in the ambiguous-object family.

title: Multi-hypothesis mask heads spend their diversity where ambiguity lives: on media they reproduce annotator distributions, on solids they collapse, giving a data-driven ambiguity taxonomy for free.
core_hypothesis: Training K-hypothesis segmentation heads on mixed data will yield hypothesis diversity concentrated on media and other boundary-undefined content, quantitatively matching multi-annotator disagreement distributions where those exist, so the trained model's diversity map doubles as an unsupervised ambiguity atlas of any dataset.

title: Scaling web data may make smoke segmentation worse: context shortcuts accumulate faster than appearance signal, so a curated controlled-capture dataset can beat orders of magnitude more scraped data on distractor-heavy tests.
core_hypothesis: As scraped smoke training data grows, in-distribution benchmark scores rise while performance on context-broken evaluations (atypical-context smoke, typical-context non-smoke) stagnates or declines, whereas a small physically controlled dataset (fog machines across many real scenes) produces better context-broken performance despite far fewer images.

title: Downsampling helps smoke segmentation: accuracy versus input resolution is non-monotone for media because high frequencies carry distractor texture but almost no smoke signal.
core_hypothesis: Smoke segmentation accuracy peaks at a moderate input resolution and declines at native resolutions because additional high-frequency content increases distractor-induced false positives without adding smoke-discriminative information, while solid-object accuracy rises monotonically over the same sweep.

title: Defocus blur dissociates media models' cue usage: smoke predictions should be blur-invariant while glass predictions collapse, and models violating this dissociation are using the wrong cues.
core_hypothesis: Because smoke evidence is low-frequency and glass evidence is concentrated in high-frequency edges and speculars, controlled defocus should leave smoke segmentation nearly intact while degrading glass segmentation sharply; models deviating from this signature (smoke performance collapsing under blur) are relying on high-frequency background texture rather than medium appearance, predicting their failures on genuinely blurry deployment footage.

title: Matting pretraining transfers to smoke better than segmentation pretraining, because the soft-boundary inductive bias matters more than semantic breadth.
core_hypothesis: At matched pretraining compute, models pretrained on alpha-matting objectives adapt to smoke segmentation faster and reach higher final quality (especially on boundary-band and thin-smoke metrics) than models pretrained on semantic segmentation, despite matting corpora being smaller and semantically narrower.

title: Sensor noise, not architecture, is the binding constraint for thin-smoke segmentation: noise-matched training recovers more thin-smoke accuracy than any recent architectural improvement.
core_hypothesis: Injecting physically calibrated sensor noise (matched to deployment cameras) during training improves thin-smoke segmentation on noisy deployment footage by more than the cumulative gains of recent architecture generations measured on the same footage, because the models' thin-smoke features are currently fitted to noise statistics they will never see again.

title: Optimizing mask quality delays alarms: mask-IoU-optimal smoke models are systematically slower to first detection than 'worse' models, an objective-level conflict in early-warning systems.
core_hypothesis: Across model pools and operating thresholds, there is a Pareto frontier between mask quality and detection latency on ignition timelines, and models at the IoU-optimal end sit far from the latency-optimal end: mask-quality selection costs meaningful detection time at fixed false-alarm budgets.

title: Untrained humans beat state-of-the-art models at incipient smoke detection via motion pop-out, indicating the missing computation is pre-attentive temporal salience, not recognition capacity.
core_hypothesis: In matched-viewing conditions (same video, same monitors, forced-choice detection), novice humans outperform current models on incipient smoke primarily due to motion-based salience, since the human advantage shrinks or vanishes on single frames and on motion-nulled videos, localizing the models' deficit to temporal salience computation rather than smoke knowledge.

title: Clutter helps glass: transparent-object segmentation may be more accurate against complex backgrounds than clean ones, inverting the universal clutter-hurts assumption.
core_hypothesis: For fixed glass objects and lighting, segmentation accuracy increases with background texture density (up to saturation) because refraction and reflection evidence scales with background structure, while opaque-object accuracy decreases over the same manipulation; current models already exploit this even though their training assumed clutter is adversity.

title: Physically correct but visually unrealistic synthetic smoke trains better models than photorealistic game-engine smoke: transfer is governed by image-formation correctness, not perceptual realism.
core_hypothesis: In a factorial synthetic-data experiment crossing perceptual realism with physical correctness of compositing (correct Beer-Lambert attenuation and scattering vs artist-tuned blending), models trained on physically correct but unrealistic-looking data transfer to real smoke better than those trained on realistic-looking but physically incorrect data, because networks key on compositing statistics rather than aesthetic properties.

title: Boundary-precision label noise is a non-problem for media: aggressive random boundary jitter in training barely hurts smoke models, exposing that annotation-precision budgets are spent on a fiction.
core_hypothesis: Training smoke segmenters with deliberately jittered boundaries (random dilation/erosion of substantial magnitude) produces models statistically indistinguishable from precisely-labeled training on all region metrics and most boundary metrics, while the same jitter substantially degrades solid-object models, quantifying how little boundary information media models actually extract from labels.

title: Models trained on composited synthetic smoke learn to detect compositing, not smoke: their real-world performance anticorrelates with their synthetic validation scores past a threshold.
core_hypothesis: Networks trained on naively composited data increasingly key on compositing artifacts (statistical seams, missing illumination coupling) as training progresses, so synthetic-validation accuracy keeps rising while real-transfer accuracy peaks early and declines, producing a measurable anticorrelation between the two curves in late training that lighting-coupled compositing eliminates.

title: A fog-machine-metered capture protocol yields physically calibrated alpha labels at scale, and one thousand physically labeled images may outtrain one hundred thousand hand-labeled ones for density-aware tasks.
core_hypothesis: Background-subtraction against pre-release reference frames plus metered fog output provides per-pixel physically defined alpha labels with negligible marginal labeling cost, and models trained on modest volumes of such data outperform models trained on far larger hand-labeled corpora on density-sensitive evaluations (transmittance ranking, threshold-family prediction), while remaining competitive on conventional mask metrics.

title: Cross-media transfer follows particle physics: generalization between fog, steam, smoke, and dust is predicted by scattering-regime similarity, giving a transfer matrix computable before any training.
core_hypothesis: The empirical transfer matrix between media segmentation tasks (train on A, test on B) is well predicted by a physical similarity computed from scattering parameters and dynamic regime, so beneficial and harmful transfers are forecastable a priori, and apparent anomalies (steam helping smoke less than fog does, or vice versa) resolve under the physical metric rather than semantic intuition.

title: The real out-of-distribution axis for fire models is flame chemistry, not scene diversity: blue, invisible, and metal-fire flames define a failure family that scene-diverse datasets never touch.
core_hypothesis: Fire segmentation models fail on chemically atypical flames (alcohol blue, hydrogen near-invisible, metal-salt colored) at rates approaching total misses regardless of scene familiarity, and augmenting training with small amounts of chemistry-diverse data recovers most of the failure, demonstrating that the operative distribution axis was chemical, not environmental.

title: Scraped fire/smoke corpora are contaminated by viral-footage near-duplicates, inflating benchmark scores through train-test leakage that perceptual-hash auditing would expose.
core_hypothesis: Near-duplicate contamination rates in scraped fire/smoke datasets substantially exceed those of general-purpose vision datasets due to viral propagation dynamics of disaster footage, and deduplicated re-evaluation measurably reduces reported scores and reorders methods, with memorization-prone (higher-capacity, longer-trained) models losing the most.

title: Generated smoke is a new deployment class: segmenters respond identically to real and diffusion-generated smoke, opening a spoofing and false-alarm channel that real-vs-generated texture statistics could close.
core_hypothesis: Current smoke segmenters respond to diffusion-generated and game-engine smoke indistinguishably from real smoke (full activation), even where generated smoke violates physical constraints (impossible illumination coupling, non-physical dynamics), meaning surveillance and monitoring pipelines can be triggered or spoofed by displayed or injected synthetic media; physically grounded consistency checks (temporal spectra, illumination coupling) can discriminate where appearance cannot.

title: Transparent-liquid dynamics are the missing hard case: static-biased glass datasets leave models helpless on pouring, splashing, and flowing water whose refractive geometry changes per frame.
core_hypothesis: Models trained on static transparency fail on dynamic liquids not gradually but categorically (treating streams as background disturbance or motion artifact), because their transparency evidence (stable rims, persistent speculars) is absent in transients; temporal integration of refraction cues, useless for static glass, becomes the dominant signal for liquids, so the static and dynamic problems require different mechanisms despite identical material.

title: Early-training label-assignment entropy predicts final detection AP better than early loss value.
core_hypothesis: The ambiguity of the assignment problem (entropy over near-equal-cost anchor/query-to-GT assignments measured in the first few epochs) captures how well the detector's supervision is structured, and is a stronger early predictor of final AP than the raw training loss at the same step.

title: One-to-one matching instability disproportionately harms small objects, explaining part of the small-object gap in end-to-end detectors.
core_hypothesis: The identity of the query matched to a given GT box flips between consecutive epochs far more often for small objects, and this matching churn (not feature resolution alone) accounts for a measurable share of the small-object AP deficit.

title: Dynamic-k assignment works mainly by enacting an implicit size-based curriculum, reproducible with a fixed size-conditioned k schedule.
core_hypothesis: The benefit of dynamic top-k positive selection comes mostly from allocating more positives to large/easy objects early and fewer to small/hard ones, i.e., an implicit curriculum indexable by object size; a static k-vs-size schedule distilled from one run reproduces most of the gain.

title: Center-biased positive sampling causes systematic under-detection of occluded objects whose visible region is off-center.
core_hypothesis: Assignment schemes that favor locations near the GT box center systematically place positives on occluder pixels when the visible fragment is off-center, teaching the model to fire on the wrong evidence; re-centering positives on the visible-region centroid improves occluded recall.

title: Assignment conflicts at object boundaries are the dominant source of classification label noise in dense detectors, and masking them beats focal-loss tuning for calibration.
core_hypothesis: Feature locations plausibly assignable to two different GT objects (or to a GT and background) receive effectively contradictory classification targets across iterations and images; excluding these conflicted locations from the classification loss removes more miscalibration than tuning the focusing parameter.

title: Soft/quality-weighted classification targets help mainly by down-weighting misassigned positives, not by providing graded supervision.
core_hypothesis: The gain from IoU-weighted soft classification targets is dominated by the suppression of low-quality (likely misassigned) positives; a hard binary mask at a quality threshold captures most of the benefit, and the graded values above threshold contribute little.

title: Assignment churn creates measurable gradient interference between classification and regression, and EMA-smoothed assignment reduces it.
core_hypothesis: When a location flips between positive and negative across iterations, its classification and regression gradients alternate in direction, producing negative cosine similarity between successive per-location gradients; smoothing the assignment decision with an EMA over iterations reduces this interference and speeds convergence.
mutation_note: The churn-to-gradient-interference measurement is the strong falsifiable core; EMA-smoothed assignment is a bolt-on fix. Mutate: lead with the instrumentation-only interference measurement and demote the EMA intervention to one validation arm.

title: One-to-many assignment's crowded-scene advantage is explained by positive-gradient mass, not by duplicate-hypothesis diversity.
core_hypothesis: The crowded-scene gap between one-to-many and one-to-one assignment is mostly a gradient-quantity effect: one-to-many delivers more positive gradient mass per GT; equalizing positive gradient mass (by loss reweighting in the one-to-one detector) eliminates most of the gap.

title: A brief deliberately-randomized assignment phase early in training reduces easy-object-first bias and improves rare-class AP.
core_hypothesis: Because early assignment costs reflect initialization noise plus easy-object signals, cost-based assignment amplifies an easy-object-first curriculum; substituting uniformly random (but geometrically valid) positive selection for the first phase of training acts as exploration and yields better rare-class and hard-object AP at equal final compute.
mutation_note: Payload as written is a training-schedule trick. Mutate: reframe around the falsifiable curriculum claim (cost-based assignment enacts an easy-object-first ordering that suppresses rare-class AP), with the randomized phase as one intervention arm among controls.

title: Where box-voting helps is predictable from per-class annotation box variance: suppressed duplicates carry complementary localization information exactly when labels are noisy.
core_hypothesis: Duplicates suppressed by NMS are approximately independent draws around the true box whose spread tracks annotation ambiguity; therefore averaging them helps most for classes whose ground-truth boxes have high annotator variance, and per-class annotation variance predicts per-class box-voting gain.

title: A per-image NMS threshold set from the pre-NMS prediction density recovers most crowd-scene AP lost to a fixed global threshold.
core_hypothesis: The NMS threshold functions as a prior over scene density; the pre-NMS score-weighted prediction density is a sufficient statistic to set that prior per image, and doing so recovers the bulk of the AP lost in dense scenes without any retraining or crowd-specific machinery.

title: Score-localization miscorrelation has two distinct modes originating in different training phases, separable by checkpoint interpolation.
core_hypothesis: Well-localized-but-low-score errors arise early (classification lags localization for hard positives) while poorly-localized-but-high-score errors arise late (classification overfits before regression saturates); interpolating between early and late checkpoints trades the two modes against each other in a predictable way.

title: Duplicate suppression in NMS-free detectors is modular: a small set of decoder components implements it and can be ablated to restore duplicates.
core_hypothesis: Duplicate suppression is implemented by a sparse, identifiable subcircuit (specific self-attention heads / decoder layers that mediate query-to-query inhibition) rather than being distributed; ablating that subcircuit selectively restores duplicate predictions while leaving single-object accuracy largely intact.

title: The score gap between a top box and its best suppressed duplicate predicts localization error better than the top score itself.
core_hypothesis: The suppressed runner-up box encodes the model's alternative hypothesis; a small score gap with high spatial disagreement indicates genuine localization ambiguity, so gap-and-disagreement statistics of suppressed duplicates outperform the raw score as a per-detection localization-error predictor.

title: Cross-class NMS suppression errors grow superlinearly with vocabulary size, becoming a first-order cost in large-vocabulary detection.
core_hypothesis: As vocabulary grows, near-synonym and part-whole class pairs proliferate faster than linearly, so class-agnostic or cross-class suppression destroys a superlinearly growing fraction of correct detections; the loss is measurable by vocabulary-subset ablation on a fixed model.

title: Learned-NMS gains are mostly context-aware rescoring, not better suppression ordering; rescoring alone captures the benefit.
core_hypothesis: The dominant effect of learned suppression modules is that they rescore boxes using scene context; if their learned scores are used only to reorder/reweight standard greedy NMS (keeping classic suppression logic), most of the AP gain survives.

title: Orientation-normalized overlap in NMS fixes a systematic suppression bias against elongated objects with zero retraining.
core_hypothesis: Because IoU between shifted copies of an elongated box decays slowly along the principal axis and quickly across it, a single IoU threshold cannot serve both axes; normalizing the overlap measure by box shape (e.g., per-axis intersection ratios) removes a shape-conditioned suppression bias measurable on existing detectors.
mutation_note: The shape-conditioned suppression-bias measurement is crisp and inference-only, but the per-axis-normalized-overlap fix lands in a crowded NMS-variant space. Mutate: measurement-first framing; any fix claim requires a prior-art sweep of shape-aware NMS variants.

title: Rising pre-NMS duplicate rate is a leading indicator of detector overfitting, preceding validation AP decline.
core_hypothesis: As a detector begins to overfit, its predictions become sharper but less consistent across nearby locations/queries, manifesting first as an increase in confident duplicates per GT on training-distribution data; this duplicate-rate inflection precedes the validation AP peak by a measurable margin.

title: NMS-free detectors wrongly self-suppress genuinely overlapping objects at a rate predictable from training-set co-occlusion statistics.
core_hypothesis: The learned inter-query inhibition in one-to-one-trained detectors generalizes the statistics of its training data: pairs of objects with overlap patterns rare in training are inhibited as if they were duplicates, so the miss rate for overlapping instance pairs is predictable from the training-set frequency of that overlap geometry and class pair.

title: IoU-based losses induce systematic box shrinkage under extent ambiguity, measurable on occluded objects.
core_hypothesis: When the true extent is ambiguous, the expected IoU-style loss is minimized by a box smaller than the mean annotation (asymmetric penalty for over- vs under-coverage under label noise), so IoU-loss-trained models exhibit a shrinkage bias on ambiguous objects that L1-trained models do not, holding data fixed.

title: Corner and center-size box parameterizations produce decorrelated errors, so cross-parameterization ensembling beats same-parameterization seed ensembling.
core_hypothesis: Center-size parameterization couples edge errors (an error in width moves two edges), while corner parameterization decouples them; the two parameterizations therefore make systematically different localization errors, and a two-model ensemble across parameterizations reduces box error more than a two-seed ensemble within one parameterization.

title: Localization error has a stride-tied quantization floor that sub-cell offset supervision removes, but only below a predictable object-size threshold.
core_hypothesis: Regression targets expressed relative to feature-cell coordinates carry an irreducible error floor proportional to the effective stride; explicitly supervising sub-cell offsets with a higher-resolution target encoding eliminates the floor, and the improvement is significant only for objects smaller than a multiple of the stride.

title: The classification-regression loss weight sets an operating point on a Pareto surface: the AP50-optimal weight measurably differs from the AP75-optimal weight.
core_hypothesis: Classification and localization capacity compete through the shared backbone; sweeping the loss weight traces a smooth Pareto front between recognition-heavy (AP50) and localization-heavy (AP75/AP90) performance, with distinct optima, so single-weight training is provably suboptimal for at least one of the two metrics.

title: Box-edge difficulty is direction-dependent and stable across architectures: ground-contact edges are systematically easier to localize.
core_hypothesis: For ground-standing object classes, the bottom edge benefits from a strong ground-plane prior and exhibits systematically lower error than the top edge (which borders variable background); this per-edge asymmetry is a stable property of the data/scene geometry, reproducing across architectures and datasets with ground-standing objects.

title: Regression-gradient conflict at features shared by overlapping objects explains a fixed share of crowded-scene localization error, removable by masked per-instance pooling.
core_hypothesis: When two GT boxes overlap, the shared feature locations receive conflicting regression targets during training, which biases both boxes toward each other; routing regression through instance-masked feature pooling (excluding the overlap region) removes this component, quantifying how much crowded-scene box error is optimization interference versus perceptual difficulty.

title: Predicted-variance regression heads help mainly through training-time loss attenuation on noisy labels; the variance output is redundant at inference.
core_hypothesis: The AP gain of variance-predicting regression comes almost entirely from down-weighting the loss on high-noise annotations during training (self-paced attenuation); discarding the variance head at inference and using standard decoding loses almost none of the gain, and the predicted variances correlate more with annotation noise proxies than with actual model error.

title: Below a predictable size threshold, plain pixel-space L1 beats IoU-family losses for tiny-object regression.
core_hypothesis: For boxes below a size threshold set by annotation noise (a few pixels of label jitter), IoU-based losses present a noise-dominated, high-curvature objective that harms optimization, while absolute-pixel L1 remains well-conditioned; a size-switched loss (L1 below threshold, IoU above) outperforms either alone, and the optimal switch point tracks the measured annotation noise scale.

title: Cascade refinement stages mostly correct one systematic scale-dependent bias each; a closed-form per-scale affine correction recovers much of the cascade gain for free.
core_hypothesis: The first-order effect of each refinement stage is to undo a systematic, scale-conditioned affine bias (shrinkage/expansion and center drift) left by the previous stage; fitting that affine correction per size band from validation statistics and applying it post hoc recovers a large fraction of cascade AP gains at zero inference cost.

title: Extreme-aspect-ratio failure is loss-induced, not representation-induced: features linearly encode the long-axis extent that IoU-loss training fails to extract.
core_hypothesis: Backbone/neck features already contain linearly decodable information about elongated objects' long-axis extent, but IoU-family losses provide vanishing gradient along the long axis (IoU is insensitive to long-axis errors relative to short-axis errors), so the head never extracts it; a frozen-feature linear probe will localize the long axis much better than the trained head does.

title: Tiny-object AP is near the label-noise ceiling: model-vs-annotator disagreement approaches annotator-vs-annotator disagreement below a size threshold.
core_hypothesis: For objects below a certain pixel size, inter-annotator box agreement degrades so much that current detectors already match the human-consistency ceiling; the remaining reported AP gap for tiny objects is largely unwinnable under the existing labels, and per-size headroom can be computed as the gap between model-annotator and annotator-annotator agreement curves.

title: Small-object detection scores oscillate with sub-stride translation due to aliasing, and anti-aliased downsampling flattens the oscillation.
core_hypothesis: Strided downsampling aliases high-frequency content that small objects depend on, making detection confidence a periodic function of sub-stride image translation; the oscillation amplitude quantifies aliasing damage, is largest for objects near the stride scale, and is substantially reduced by anti-aliased (low-pass-filtered) downsampling at matched accuracy elsewhere.

title: Top-down FPN fusion oversmooths the finest pyramid level, measurably erasing high-frequency discriminability that small objects need.
core_hypothesis: After top-down fusion, the finest-level features lose high-spatial-frequency discriminative information present before fusion (measurable by frequency-band-restricted linear probes for small-object presence); gating the fusion by frequency (letting high-frequency content bypass the smoothing) recovers small-object AP without hurting large objects.

title: Small objects are recognized mostly from context while large objects are recognized from appearance, and interior-vs-context masking reverses between the two regimes.
core_hypothesis: Below a size threshold, detection decisions rely mainly on surrounding context (object pixels contribute less than their surround); masking the object interior hurts small-object detection less than masking an equal-area context ring, with the effect reversing for large objects, and the crossover size is a stable architecture property.

title: Per-class test-time resolution selection beats any single global resolution because class-wise resolution-AP curves peak at different points.
core_hypothesis: Class-conditional resolution-AP curves have materially different optima (driven by each class's size distribution and texture frequency); running inference at 2-3 resolutions and reading each class's detections from its best resolution yields an aggregate AP above the best single resolution, and the per-class optima are predictable from class size statistics alone.
mutation_note: Keep the falsifiable claim that class-conditional resolution-AP optima diverge and are predictable from class size statistics; drop the per-class selection system as the contribution - multi-scale/selective inference is well-trodden engineering.

title: Scale augmentation works by renormalizing objects into a fixed preferred absolute-pixel band, not by teaching scale invariance.
core_hypothesis: Detectors have an architecture-determined preferred absolute object-size band (in pixels at the input); scale augmentation helps mainly because it moves more training (and effectively test) objects through that band, not because the model becomes scale-invariant; consequently per-scale AP measured in absolute pixels retains a fixed peak whose location is unchanged by augmentation strength while its width grows only modestly.

title: Tiling-based small-object gains come substantially from activation-statistics changes, not just effective resolution; matched-statistics full-image inference closes much of the gap.
core_hypothesis: Part of tiling's small-object improvement arises because tiles present object-denser, background-simpler statistics to normalization layers and global operators; reproducing those statistics on full images (e.g., normalization recalibrated to tile statistics, attention temperature adjusted) recovers a meaningful fraction of tiling's gain without the resolution change or the border-artifact costs.

title: Small-object skill peaks earlier in training and is forgotten first under continued or fine-tuning updates: a scale-dependent forgetting curve.
core_hypothesis: Small-object accuracy behaves like a fragile, high-frequency skill: it reaches its optimum earlier than large-object accuracy during training, and degrades first when training continues (overfit) or when fine-tuning on a shifted distribution; therefore single-checkpoint selection systematically sacrifices small-object AP, and scale-wise checkpoint blending strictly dominates.

title: Learned features preserve sub-stride localization information for small objects that standard decoding discards: a readout can beat the stride bound.
core_hypothesis: Distributed activation patterns across neighboring feature cells retain sub-stride positional information (analogous to population coding); a lightweight multi-cell readout trained on frozen stride-8/16 features can localize small objects with error well below the naive stride bound, showing the bottleneck is the decoding head, not the encoded information.

title: Detection scores are a range-dependent mixture of three latent factors, and the mixture map predicts where each calibration method works.
core_hypothesis: A detection score mixes classification correctness, localization quality, and duplicate-rank information, with mixture weights that vary systematically across score ranges (e.g., top scores dominated by duplicate rank, mid scores by classification); estimating the range-dependent mixture explains and predicts which score ranges each calibration method (temperature, isotonic, IoU-aware rescoring) can and cannot fix.

title: Per-class calibration error in detectors follows a class-frequency scaling law, so a single frequency-parameterized correction nearly matches per-class tuning.
core_hypothesis: The dominant driver of per-class miscalibration is training-set class frequency (through imbalance in positive gradients and background competition); calibration error versus log-frequency follows a smooth monotone law, so a two-parameter frequency-conditioned temperature achieves calibration close to per-class tuning while needing no rare-class validation data.

title: Cross-domain score-threshold failure is driven by background shift, and label-free recalibration on background-only patches restores threshold validity.
core_hypothesis: The score distribution shift that invalidates thresholds across domains originates mostly from changed background statistics (new negatives) rather than changed object appearance; therefore recalibrating the score scale using only target-domain background regions (obtainable without object labels, e.g., from detector-quiet regions or known object-free footage) restores most threshold transferability.

title: Out-of-distribution false positives have systematically unstable box geometry under input jitter, enabling training-free OOD rejection.
core_hypothesis: For in-distribution objects, the regression head has learned a stable attractor (box estimates are consistent under small input perturbations), whereas confident OOD false positives sit off the learned manifold and their boxes wander under jitter; box-consistency-under-jitter therefore separates OOD FPs from true detections better than any function of the classification logits alone.

title: Box-level and image-level calibration diverge systematically: a detector can be well calibrated per box yet badly calibrated for 'any object present' image queries.
core_hypothesis: Aggregating box scores into image-level probabilities (e.g., via max or noisy-or) inherits correlations between per-box errors within an image, so box-level calibration does not imply image-level calibration; the divergence grows with per-image detection count and error correlation, and direct image-level recalibration beats aggregating box-calibrated scores.

title: Detection score rankings are far more seed-stable than score values, so rank-based thresholds transfer better than calibrated-score thresholds.
core_hypothesis: Across random seeds (and minor recipe changes), the induced ranking of detections is substantially more stable than the score values themselves; consequently thresholds expressed as per-image or per-dataset rank/quantile statistics transfer across retrains with less operating-point drift than value thresholds, even after post-hoc calibration of the values.

title: Focal loss's calibration damage is temporally separable from its accuracy benefit: a brief final cross-entropy phase restores calibration at no AP cost.
core_hypothesis: The accuracy benefit of focusing (hard-example emphasis) is realized in representation and localization quality accumulated over training, while the calibration distortion lives in the final classifier layer's output scaling; switching to plain cross-entropy (or reduced focusing) only for the final small fraction of training re-anchors output probabilities without unwinding the learned representations, keeping AP while removing most calibration error.
mutation_note: The representation/final-layer separability hypothesis must beat the trivial null: temperature scaling already re-anchors output scaling post hoc (the shard's own protocol includes it). Mutate: surviving claim is advantage over post-hoc recalibration under shift; otherwise dominated.

title: IoU-prediction heads mostly re-encode class and size priors; their instance-specific quality signal is small and measurable by a prior-only baseline.
core_hypothesis: Most of the variance in predicted IoU is explained by class identity and box size (which correlate with typical achievable IoU), not by instance-specific evidence; a baseline predicting quality from (class, size, image-level difficulty) alone will match the head's correlation with true IoU closely, revealing a small residual instance signal.

title: False negatives are more predictable than false positives from internal features, enabling a practical 'missed something here' flag.
core_hypothesis: Images and regions where a detector misses objects have identifiable internal signatures (elevated objectness without box commitment, feature-space proximity to positives, high spatial entropy of low-level saliency vs low detection density); a lightweight predictor on frozen intermediate features flags FN-containing regions with usefully high precision, and FN-predictability exceeds FP-predictability under matched effort.

title: Score-distribution degradation under diverse corruptions collapses onto a single 'effective dose' scalar per model, enabling corruption-agnostic monitoring.
core_hypothesis: For a fixed detector, the changes in its detection-score distribution under many different corruption types lie on a one-dimensional family: each (type, severity) maps to a scalar effective dose, and score-distribution statistics identify the dose regardless of corruption type; consequently, a monitor calibrated on a few synthetic corruptions predicts AP degradation for unseen corruption types from the score distribution alone.

title: Detection heads are systematically under-trained relative to backbones: a final frozen-backbone, high-LR head phase yields consistent gains.
core_hypothesis: Because head targets keep shifting while assignment and features co-adapt, heads end training away from their optimum for the final feature distribution; freezing the backbone at the end and continuing head-only training at elevated LR (retargeting heads to now-stationary features) adds AP reliably, reversing the usual fine-tuning intuition that heads adapt quickly and backbones need care.
mutation_note: Head-only retraining closely resembles decoupled classifier-retraining practice. Mutate: the idea is the measurable head/backbone convergence mismatch under assignment non-stationarity, not the retuning recipe; frame the recipe as the confirmation experiment.

title: Classification and localization peak at different training epochs; per-task checkpoint blending beats the best single checkpoint.
core_hypothesis: Classification quality (correct labels, ranking) and localization quality (box accuracy) follow different training trajectories with systematically offset optima; constructing a model whose classification pathway comes from one epoch and regression pathway from another (weight-blend or head-swap) outperforms every single checkpoint of the run.

title: 'Longer detection training hurts transfer' is driven by background-logit sharpening, and background-entropy regularization preserves transferability at no in-domain cost.
core_hypothesis: Extended training primarily sharpens the background decision (negative logits grow confident on dataset-specific background textures), which is the least transferable component; the foreground representations keep improving or plateau. A regularizer keeping background predictive entropy high preserves transfer performance without sacrificing in-domain AP, and background-logit sharpness measured over training predicts transfer degradation.

title: Assignment adaptivity corrupts the validation loss as a model-selection signal; assignment-frozen validation loss tracks AP better late in training.
core_hypothesis: Because the assignment procedure re-solves per evaluation, a model can lower measured loss by shifting which predictions get matched (gaming the matching) without improving actual detection quality; freezing the assignment (computing loss against a fixed, precomputed matching from a reference checkpoint) removes this degree of freedom and yields a loss that rank-correlates with AP substantially better in mid-to-late training.

title: Large-batch detection training should scale LR by positive-instance count, not image count: gradient noise is set by positives per batch.
core_hypothesis: The effective gradient noise scale in detection is governed by the number of positive instances per batch (few per image, heavy-tailed across images), not the image count; therefore LR should scale with expected positive count, and batch construction that equalizes positives across batches (instance-balanced batching) improves large-batch stability and final AP over image-count-based scaling.

title: Repeating a rare-class instance within one batch is worth less than across batches: shared-feature gradient coupling suppresses same-batch repetition gains.
