core_hypothesis: Multiple copies of the same rare instance in one batch produce highly correlated gradients through shared weights that the optimizer treats as one large step (with clipped/normalized effects), while the same copies spread over consecutive batches interact with different negatives and momentum states, yielding better rare-class learning; thus repeat-factor sampling schedules that spread copies temporally beat within-batch duplication at equal copy budget.

title: Mosaic-style augmentation gains are mostly a positive-density effect: density-matched conventional sampling closes most of the gap.
core_hypothesis: The dominant benefit of mosaic-like composition is simply more GT instances per gradient step (higher supervised signal density); a baseline that matches positives-per-iteration by batching more images (or cropping object-dense regions) without composition recovers most of the gain, leaving only a small residual attributable to context/scale mixing.

title: EMA's detection benefit concentrates in the regression branch; EMA-ing only neck and box head captures most of the gain.
core_hypothesis: The regression pathway suffers more from late-training weight oscillation (its loss landscape is more anisotropic due to box-scale heterogeneity), so EMA's benefit is disproportionately a localization-smoothing effect; component-selective EMA (neck + regression head only) achieves most of full-model EMA's AP gain, while cls-head-only EMA is nearly neutral.

title: Warmup length in detection is dictated by assignment stabilization, not LR safety: stabilize assignment and warmup can shrink drastically.
core_hypothesis: Early training divergence in detectors is triggered by feedback between fast-changing predictions and cost-based assignment (assignment amplifies prediction noise into label noise); with assignment stabilized early (geometric-prior-based or EMA-smoothed assignment for the first phase), full LR can be applied almost immediately without divergence, showing that warmup was protecting the assignment loop rather than the optimizer.

title: Seed-to-seed AP variance is concentrated in an identifiable set of 'swing images', predictable from a single run's internal signals.
core_hypothesis: Cross-seed AP variance is dominated by a small subset of images whose scoring sits near assignment/NMS/threshold decision boundaries (high-ambiguity scenes); these swing images are identifiable from a single trained model via internal ambiguity signals (score margins, duplicate structure, matching cost gaps), enabling variance prediction and variance-adjusted comparisons without training extra seeds.

title: Datasets mix modal and amodal box conventions inconsistently per class, and per-class convention consistency predicts per-class AP75.
core_hypothesis: Within standard detection datasets, the modal/amodal choice for occluded instances varies by annotator and by class in measurable proportions; models learn a per-class average convention, and classes with more internally inconsistent conventions have systematically lower AP75 after controlling for size, frequency, and occlusion rate.

title: Ignore-region training creates blind spots that generalize beyond the ignored regions to visually similar non-ignored areas.
core_hypothesis: Excluding regions from the loss does not make them neutral: because ignored regions share appearance statistics (dense crowds, clutter), the model receives systematically censored supervision for that appearance class and learns reduced detection propensity there; consequently detection recall in non-ignored areas that resemble typical ignore-region appearance is measurably depressed.

title: Missing annotations concentrate near image borders and small scales, making border 'false positives' disproportionately genuine detections.
core_hypothesis: Annotation misses are not uniform: they cluster at image borders, partial visibility, and small scales; therefore high-confidence detector 'false positives' in those strata are enriched for true objects, and re-reviewing only border/small FPs yields a much higher label-correction rate than reviewing random FPs, with consequences for training (hard-negative mining corrupts exactly there) and evaluation (border-heavy methods are unfairly penalized).

title: Mid-training checkpoints are better annotation-error detectors than converged models, which have already memorized the errors.
core_hypothesis: There is a mid-training sweet spot where a detector has learned the true data patterns but not yet memorized annotation errors; model-GT disagreements at this stage have substantially higher precision for genuine label errors than disagreements from the final checkpoint, and the sweet spot is identifiable from training dynamics (before the train-clean/train-noisy loss gap closes).

title: Fine-grained sibling classes cause score-mass splitting rather than misclassification, and sibling-aware aggregation recovers the lost detections.
core_hypothesis: For visually confusable sibling classes, detectors distribute score mass across the siblings (two medium scores instead of one high score); after thresholding/NMS this manifests as missed detections rather than wrong-class detections, so aggregating scores over sibling groups before thresholding recovers objects that per-class scoring loses, improving group-level recall at no precision cost.

title: Duplicate ground-truth annotations destabilize one-to-one matching training measurably more than one-to-many, and a duplicate audit predicts which images hurt.
core_hypothesis: Under one-to-one bipartite matching, duplicate GTs force the model to produce two distinct predictions for one object, directly contradicting the learned self-suppression objective and injecting persistent gradient conflict; under one-to-many assignment the duplicates largely merge into the same positive set, so the damage is much smaller. Per-image training-loss volatility will therefore flag duplicate-GT images in one-to-one training specifically.

title: Annotators snap boxes to high-contrast edges rather than true object extents, and models inherit a measurable contrast-seeking localization bias.
core_hypothesis: Human-drawn boxes systematically align with strong image gradients even when the object extends beyond them (shadows, low-contrast parts, transparent regions); models trained on such labels reproduce the bias, predicting boxes that snap to contrast edges; the bias is measurable by comparing predicted boxes on objects with deliberately low-contrast extensions (synthetic composites) where the true extent is known.

title: Detectors average synthetic box-label noise for large objects but not below a size threshold, defining a label-quality-dominated regime.
core_hypothesis: When box labels carry zero-mean jitter, the learned regressor averages the noise effectively for objects large relative to the jitter scale (many correlated examples, smooth interpolation), but below a size threshold the noise is effectively multiplicative and learning degrades sharply; therefore there exists a measurable size-dependent noise-robustness curve with a knee, and labeling precision only matters below the knee.

title: At the margin, certified object-free regions ('verified negatives') buy more detection quality per annotation dollar than additional positive boxes.
core_hypothesis: Much of the FP rate and score miscalibration of mature detectors stems from uncertainty about whether unlabeled regions are truly negative (missing-label ambiguity); a modest budget spent certifying regions as object-free (cheap per unit area) provides clean negative supervision whose marginal value, in a mature-training regime, exceeds the marginal value of the same budget spent on additional positive boxes.

title: Method rankings flip between mAP and fixed-precision recall often enough to change practical conclusions, and the flips are predictable from score-distribution shape.
core_hypothesis: Because mAP rewards long low-confidence tails while deployments never see them, pairs of detectors frequently invert order between mAP and recall-at-fixed-precision; the inversion probability is predictable from the divergence of their score-distribution shapes (tail-heavy vs concentrated), enabling a cheap flag for 'this mAP comparison will not transfer to deployment'.

title: AP can be gamed measurably by score-tail shaping without changing any decision-relevant prediction, exposing a metric integrity flaw.
core_hypothesis: Manipulating only the low-confidence tail (adding hallucinated near-zero-score boxes in strategic locations, reordering ties, per-class score monotone transforms) changes measured AP by margins comparable to publishable 'improvements', while every fixed-threshold operating point above practical confidence remains identical; the exploit size varies by AP implementation and per-class instance counts.

title: Class-averaged mAP misallocates model capacity relative to downstream utility, and instance-weighted AP reranks models in a utility-aligned way.
core_hypothesis: Model rankings under class-equal mAP and instance-frequency-weighted AP diverge materially, and for common downstream aggregate tasks (counting, indexing, alerting on any object) the instance-weighted metric predicts realized utility better; some 'state-of-the-art' differences reflect rare-class score arbitrage rather than broadly better detection.
mutation_note: 'Predicts realized utility better' hinges on contestable utility simulations - conceded in main_risk. Mutate: restrict to the crisp, cheap core (rankings materially diverge between class-equal and instance-weighted AP, driven by rare-class score arbitrage).

title: The discrete IoU-threshold ladder in AP misses real localization improvements that a continuous localization metric detects with higher statistical power.
core_hypothesis: Two models can differ meaningfully in localization (mean matched IoU, tail box errors) while their thresholded AP values are statistically indistinguishable at feasible test-set sizes; a continuous metric (e.g., expected matched IoU or signed-error distributions) detects such differences with substantially higher power, and some published-scale architecture differences are of exactly this hidden kind.

title: Cross-dataset detector rankings are unstable under reasonable alternative class-mapping choices, making label-space mapping a hidden researcher degree of freedom.
core_hypothesis: For typical dataset pairs, multiple defensible class mappings exist (synonym scope, part-whole choices, granularity merges), and detector rankings change across these mappings often enough that some cross-dataset generalization claims are mapping artifacts; the sensitivity is measurable as ranking variance over an enumerated space of defensible mappings.

title: A matched error-decomposition shows architectures differ mainly in one error type each, which aggregate AP deltas systematically mis-attribute.
core_hypothesis: When errors are decomposed with a consistent matched protocol (each GT and prediction assigned to exactly one error category), major architecture families exhibit signature error profiles (e.g., one family trades duplicates for misses, another trades localization for classification); most pairwise AP gaps are dominated by a single category, so category-targeted fixes could equalize families at far lower cost than adopting new architectures.

title: A cut-paste out-of-context evaluation isolates context reliance as a stable per-architecture scalar that standard AP conflates with recognition ability.
core_hypothesis: Evaluating detectors on a controlled companion set where objects are composited into unfamiliar-but-plausible contexts yields a context-reliance score (in-context AP minus out-of-context AP, artifact-controlled); this score varies widely across architectures at matched standard AP and predicts robustness to natural distribution shifts better than standard AP does.

title: Categorical size buckets (small/medium/large) create boundary artifacts; continuous size-AP curves reveal crossovers that bucket metrics hide.
core_hypothesis: Model comparisons using bucketed size metrics mask crossover structure: one model can dominate another everywhere except a narrow size band (or vice versa) with identical bucket summaries; continuous AP-versus-size curves (kernel-smoothed matched-recall/precision) expose such crossovers, and for some checkpoint pairs the bucket verdict and the continuous-curve verdict disagree in practically relevant size ranges.

title: Resolution-mismatch sensitivity is a stable, rankable model property that standard fixed-resolution evaluation never measures.
core_hypothesis: Detectors differ systematically and stably in how gracefully AP degrades as inference resolution departs from training resolution (a 'resolution robustness' curve shaped by architecture and augmentation, consistent across datasets); two models with equal native-resolution AP can differ dramatically off-resolution, and the robustness curve rank is preserved across datasets, making it a legitimate reportable model property.

title: Score-free ranking metrics (recall versus detections-per-image curves) are more seed- and domain-stable than AP, making them better low-budget model selectors.
core_hypothesis: Metrics that depend only on the ranking of detections (e.g., recall at k detections per image, area under recall-vs-budget curves) strip away score-scale artifacts and are therefore more stable across random seeds and more predictive of large-set AP and cross-domain AP than small-sample AP itself is.

title: Detectors compress background rejection into a small set of feature-space prototypes whose drift predicts false-positive spikes under domain shift, label-free.
core_hypothesis: Negative decisions in a trained detector are mediated by a compact set of background prototypes (clusters in feature space covering most rejected locations); when a new domain's background features fall outside prototype coverage, rejection fails; therefore a coverage statistic computed on unlabeled target images predicts the FP increase before any labels exist.

title: Classes split bimodally into context-dependent and appearance-dependent groups, and the split predicts which classes cut-paste augmentation helps versus harms.
core_hypothesis: Per-class context reliance (measured by in-context vs out-of-context detection gap) is bimodal rather than continuous: classes are either context-anchored (small, ambiguous, habitual-location objects) or appearance-anchored; cut-paste augmentation improves appearance-anchored classes' robustness but actively degrades context-anchored classes' accuracy by destroying their primary evidence channel, making the reliance measurement a pre-training predictor of per-class augmentation outcome.

title: Co-occurrence priors live in the classification head, not the features: head transplantation moves context bias between detectors.
core_hypothesis: Object co-occurrence and scene-prior effects are implemented predominantly in the classification head's weighting of context-carrying feature channels, while backbone/neck features remain relatively context-neutral; transplanting the head from a context-biased model onto a context-neutral model's features (with light adapter alignment) transfers the measured context bias, and vice versa, localizing the bias to the head.

title: Negative context (scene-based implausibility) contributes more to detector precision than positive context contributes to recall - an exploitable asymmetry.
core_hypothesis: Detectors use scene evidence asymmetrically: suppression of contextually implausible candidates (negative context) is a stronger, more reliable effect than enhancement of contextually plausible ones (positive context); intervention studies (inserting objects into implausible scenes vs removing supportive context around plausible ones) will quantify a suppression-dominance ratio above one, implying that context-debiasing for open-world recall should target the suppression pathway specifically.

title: Part-whole false positives (detecting a wheel as a car, a face as a person) are removable by a training-free containment-consistency test.
core_hypothesis: Part-whole FPs have a structural signature: the false 'whole' detection is spatially contained in (or contains) a higher-evidence detection of the related category, with characteristic size ratios; a post-hoc consistency test over the detection set (checking containment relations against a small learned or hand-specified part-whole relation table) removes a large fraction of these FPs at negligible true-positive cost, without retraining.

title: Physical-artifact false positives (shadows, reflections, prints) share a single cross-class feature-space direction, enabling one-vector debiasing.
core_hypothesis: The features of artifact-triggered detections differ from real-object detections along a low-dimensional, class-shared direction (encoding cues like missing 3D shading structure, boundary inconsistency, or surface context); a single linear direction fitted on artifact examples from a few classes will separate artifact FPs in unseen classes too, and projecting it out (or thresholding along it) reduces artifact FPs broadly at minor TP cost.

title: Detectors carry a learned per-image object-count prior that suppresses detections in dense scenes and inflates them in sparse ones.
core_hypothesis: Training distributions concentrate object counts in a moderate range; detectors internalize this as a soft prior on total detections per image (via global feature pathways and score normalization effects), so per-image predicted counts regress toward the training mode: dense scenes are under-counted beyond what per-object difficulty explains, and near-empty scenes over-counted; conditioning score calibration on estimated scene density counteracts the prior and improves both tails.

title: Inter-object score interference is asymmetric by size: adding a large object suppresses nearby small-object scores far more than the reverse.
core_hypothesis: Feature pooling, attention normalization, and suppression stages make each detection's score depend on other objects present, and the dependence is size-asymmetric: large objects capture shared feature capacity and attention mass, measurably suppressing nearby small-object scores, while small objects barely affect large ones; the interference decays with distance on a characteristic length scale that differs by architecture family.

title: Background texture entropy predicts per-image false-positive count better than object count or image size, enabling entropy-adaptive thresholds.
core_hypothesis: FP generation is driven primarily by background texture complexity (entropy/edge density of non-object regions offering more spurious pattern matches), not by scene object count or resolution; a cheap texture-entropy statistic predicts per-image FP counts well, and an entropy-conditioned score threshold improves image-level precision at fixed aggregate recall over any global threshold.

title: Test-time augmentation benefit is predictable per model from a training-augmentation saturation score: TTA is redundant augmentation.
core_hypothesis: TTA (flips, multi-scale) helps exactly to the degree that the model failed to internalize the corresponding invariance during training; a cheap 'augmentation saturation' score (agreement between the model's outputs on augmented input pairs, measured on unlabeled data) therefore predicts each model's TTA gain, with strongly augmented modern recipes near saturation (TTA wasted) and lightly augmented models below it (TTA valuable).

title: Video detection flicker is mostly score oscillation around the threshold, not feature instability; temporal score smoothing alone removes most of it.
core_hypothesis: For static or slowly moving objects, the underlying localization and features are frame-stable; flicker arises because scores hover near the operating threshold and cross it with per-frame noise; consequently exponential smoothing of matched detection scores across frames (no feature-level temporal modeling, no tracking beyond greedy IoU matching) eliminates the majority of identity flicker at negligible compute, bounding the value of temporal feature architectures for this specific failure mode.

title: Quantization degrades localization before classification: box quality collapses at bit-widths where class accuracy still holds, motivating branch-asymmetric precision.
core_hypothesis: Box regression outputs are continuous and sensitive to activation resolution, while classification decisions have wide margins; therefore, as weights/activations are quantized more aggressively, localization error (AP75, matched IoU) degrades earlier and faster than classification accuracy, and allocating higher precision only to the regression pathway (head and last neck stage) recovers most full-precision AP at nearly the low-precision compute cost.

title: A small identifiable subset of normalization layers causes batch-size-1 inference score shifts, with object-size-dependent effects fixable by targeted statistic freezing.
core_hypothesis: The train-to-deployment statistic mismatch is concentrated: a small subset of normalization layers (those whose activation statistics vary most with scene composition) accounts for most of the score shift, and the shift is object-size-dependent (small-object scores move most because their evidence is normalization-sensitive); freezing or recalibrating only the culprit layers removes most of the shift, preserving whatever adaptivity the rest provide.

title: Recall degrades in discrete stair-steps as inference resolution drops, aligned with stride-boundary crossings of object pixel sizes, so deployment resolutions should snap to critical points.
core_hypothesis: As input resolution decreases, cohorts of objects cross assignment/pyramid-level boundaries together (their pixel sizes fall below per-level minima), producing stair-step drops in recall at predictable resolutions determined by the object-size distribution and the model's stride/level configuration; between steps, resolution reductions are nearly free, so latency tuning should jump between step edges rather than sample the dial uniformly.

title: Motion-blur 'detection failure' is substantially a localization-convention mismatch: models find blurred objects but place boxes at the blur centroid while annotations follow sharp-frame conventions.
core_hypothesis: Under motion blur, a meaningful fraction of measured failure is not missed recognition but box-placement disagreement: the physically ambiguous extent of a blurred object (leading edge vs trailing edge vs centroid) is resolved differently by models and by annotation conventions, so IoU-based matching fails despite successful detection; evaluating with blur-aware matching (relaxed or convention-normalized along the motion axis) recovers a substantial fraction of the apparent robustness gap.

title: Per-image difficulty-based resolution routing beats any fixed-resolution configuration on the AP-per-FLOP frontier, and difficulty is predictable from cheap image features.
core_hypothesis: Per-image detection difficulty (whether high resolution changes the outcome) is predictable from cheap covariates (thumbnail-based small-object likelihood, edge density, a tiny proxy model's confidence profile); routing only predicted-hard images to high resolution achieves a strictly better AP-versus-compute frontier than every fixed resolution, with the routing predictor requiring orders of magnitude less compute than the savings it enables.
mutation_note: Oracle headroom plus predictability-of-difficulty is the falsifiable core and dies cheaply on a null. Building the router is standard dynamic-resolution engineering; cut the routing system from the claim.

title: Ensemble gains in detection are predictable from single-model score-gap statistics: disagreement lives on a stable ambiguity set visible to one model.
core_hypothesis: Detector ensemble improvements concentrate on a stable subset of objects characterized by intra-model ambiguity signals (small top-score margins, duplicate structure, unstable boxes under jitter); because these signals are measurable on one model, the achievable ensemble gain (and where it will land - which classes, sizes, scene types) is predictable before building the ensemble, within a useful tolerance.

title: In streaming detection, latency jitter (variance) degrades effective accuracy more than equal-mean latency increase: stability beats speed near real-time thresholds.
core_hypothesis: For dynamic scenes, the accuracy cost of a late result grows superlinearly with delay (objects move, matches expire), so a latency distribution's variance contributes disproportionately to streaming detection error: a configuration with slightly higher mean but low jitter (e.g., fixed compute paths, reserved resources) outperforms a faster-on-average but jittery configuration in streaming metrics, and the crossover is predictable from scene motion statistics.

title: High-norm outlier tokens in CLIP-style ViTs, not decoder design, are the primary bottleneck for training-free open-vocabulary segmentation.
core_hypothesis: A small set of high-norm 'attention sink' patch tokens carry global rather than local information and dominate patch-text similarity maps; suppressing or imputing them recovers most of the quality currently attributed to sophisticated training-free decoders.

title: VLM patch embeddings encode global image gist more than local patch content, and this 'patch leakage' bounds dense transfer.
core_hypothesis: In contrastively trained VLMs, a linear probe can decode the whole-image class from a single patch embedding more accurately than that patch's own local content, and the ratio of global-to-local decodability predicts dense transfer quality across backbones.

title: For some classes, VLM similarity maps peak on co-occurring background rather than the object, making errors anti-correlated with the object, not random.
core_hypothesis: Contrastive alignment binds words to whole scenes, so for context-dependent classes the patch-text similarity is systematically higher on the co-occurring background; a per-class 'anti-grounding' score is stable across datasets and predicts which classes benefit from context-suppression fixes.

title: Dense-relevant information in VLM encoders peaks at intermediate layers, and layer selection matters more than adapter architecture for dense transfer.
core_hypothesis: The final layers of contrastive VLMs specialize toward the global alignment objective and discard spatial detail, so a probing curve over depth is non-monotonic for dense tasks; choosing the best intermediate layer yields larger gains than switching among adapter designs applied to the final layer.

title: Patch-embedding norms in VLMs encode class-agnostic objectness well enough to rival learned mask-proposal stages.
core_hypothesis: Because contrastive training pushes informative regions to higher feature magnitude, simple functions of patch norm (possibly after outlier removal) provide objectness maps whose proposal recall approaches trained proposal networks, without any dense supervision.

title: Contrastive pretraining buys translation invariance at the price of boundary precision, and the deficit is objective-specific rather than resolution-specific.
core_hypothesis: In-batch contrastive objectives reward local translation invariance, measurably blurring boundary-adjacent feature transitions; at matched resolution and patch size, contrastive VLMs will show a larger boundary-versus-interior quality gap than dense-supervised or reconstruction-pretrained models.

title: Patch-level text alignment in VLMs emerges discontinuously with scale, unlike smoothly improving image-level alignment.
core_hypothesis: Zero-shot dense metrics across a family of checkpoints spanning model and data scale will show threshold-like emergence (near-flat then rapid rise), whereas zero-shot classification improves smoothly, implying dense usefulness cannot be predicted from classification-scale curves.

title: Anisotropy of VLM patch-feature space, not prompt quality, limits zero-shot dense prediction, and simple whitening beats prompt ensembling.
core_hypothesis: VLM patch embeddings occupy a narrow anisotropic cone that compresses class-discriminative directions; whitening patch features with statistics from unlabeled images enlarges effective angular separation and improves zero-shot segmentation more than prompt ensembling does.

title: Open-vocabulary segmentation rankings are unstable under synonym substitution of class names, revealing lexical rather than semantic grounding.
core_hypothesis: Replacing class names with common synonyms changes per-class IoU by more than typical method-to-method differences, and method rankings computed under different synonym choices disagree materially.

title: Prompt templates inherited from classification are systematically suboptimal for dense prediction, and the optimal template differs by class type.
core_hypothesis: Templates describing regions, materials, or partial views align better with patch-level features than whole-image templates, and the gap is larger for stuff classes than thing classes, because captions describe whole scenes while patches depict parts.

title: The stuff-class performance gap in open-vocabulary segmentation is primarily a text-encoder deficiency, not a vision-feature deficiency.
core_hypothesis: Text encoders trained on object-centric captions represent mass nouns (grass, pavement, water) in a degenerate region of embedding space; substituting better text-side representations while freezing vision features closes a large fraction of the stuff-thing gap.

title: Fine-grained open-vocabulary dense prediction collapses to basic-level categories because hypernym similarity dominates class-name embeddings.
core_hypothesis: Text embeddings of fine-grained names are dominated by their hypernym component, so patch similarities barely distinguish siblings; confusion mass flows toward basic-level categories beyond what visual confusability predicts.

title: Tokenization length of a class name is an independent predictor of its open-vocabulary dense performance, beyond frequency and visual difficulty.
core_hypothesis: Names splitting into more subword tokens produce noisier text embeddings, and this measurably reduces dense performance after controlling for name frequency and object size; single-token aliases recover part of the loss.

title: Learned 'background' embeddings in open-vocabulary segmentation do not transfer across vocabularies, making rejection quality an unmeasured failure mode.
core_hypothesis: The learned background embedding encodes 'not in my training vocabulary' rather than 'not in the current query set', so rejection quality collapses when the deployed vocabulary differs from the training one, in either direction (larger or smaller).

title: Bag-of-words behavior of VLM text encoders imposes a hard ceiling on dense tasks requiring syntax, measurable by word-order perturbation invariance.
core_hypothesis: For dense systems built on contrastive text towers, output masks are largely invariant to meaning-changing word-order permutations of the query, and the degree of this invariance predicts the system's failure rate on relation-critical referring expressions.

title: Dense grounding of spatial relations is driven by object priors, not relations: predictions barely change when the stated relation is inverted.
core_hypothesis: For VLM-based referring segmentation, swapping the relation word ('left of' to 'right of') changes the predicted mask in only a small minority of cases where the swap should change the referent, and success cases are explained by single-candidate scenes.

title: VLM dense grounding defaults to viewer-centric frames of reference and cannot switch to object-centric frames on request.
core_hypothesis: Dense predictions for object-centric spatial expressions match viewer-centric interpretations at well above chance, indicating the frame is hard-coded by dataset statistics rather than parsed from language; mirrored-image tests expose the bias cleanly.

title: Numerals in dense-prediction prompts do not modulate how many instances get segmented, revealing that count words are treated as noise.
core_hypothesis: Open-vocabulary and referring segmenters produce statistically indistinguishable instance counts for prompts differing only in the numeral, and their masks do not preferentially cover numeral-consistent subsets.

title: Ordinal references ('second from the left') are resolved by saliency rank, not positional rank, in VLM dense grounding.
core_hypothesis: When positional rank and visual saliency rank disagree, dense models select the referent by saliency; error patterns will follow the saliency ordering rather than being uniform.

title: Size comparatives in dense grounding are resolved by pixel area rather than inferred physical size, failing under perspective.
core_hypothesis: VLM referring systems ground size comparatives by projected pixel area; on scenes where perspective inverts apparent size (the physically larger object is farther and smaller in the image), accuracy on size comparatives will invert accordingly.

title: Per-relation grounding accuracy is predicted by caption-corpus frequency of the relational construction, not by its geometric complexity.
core_hypothesis: The ordering of relations by dense-grounding accuracy matches their construction frequency in web caption corpora more closely than any geometry-based difficulty measure, implying relation grounding is memorized from language statistics rather than computed.

title: Referring segmentation models almost never abstain: they emit confident masks even when the referent is absent from the image.
core_hypothesis: Standard referring segmenters produce masks with confidence statistics indistinguishable from present-referent cases when given absent-referent prompts, because no component of the architecture models existence; abstention requires an explicit existence head, not thresholding.

title: Open-vocabulary detectors produce more false positives on object-free images than closed-vocabulary counterparts at matched recall, and the gap grows with vocabulary size.
core_hypothesis: Querying many text embeddings against every location makes false-positive rate scale with vocabulary size for open-vocabulary detectors, a structural cost of text-query architectures that closed-vocabulary heads do not pay.

title: Query-order and query-set composition bias per-class dense predictions: the same class scores differently depending on which other classes are queried alongside it.
core_hypothesis: Per-class IoU/AP shifts materially when the surrounding vocabulary changes (adding distractors, removing rivals), and part of published cross-method differences is actually differences in vocabulary composition handling rather than grounding quality.

title: Activation maps for pseudo-words (nonsense tokens) predict where dense VLMs will hallucinate real absent objects.
core_hypothesis: Querying a VLM dense system with meaningless pseudo-words yields activation concentrated on high-genericity object regions, and these maps overlap strongly with where real absent-category queries produce false masks, revealing a query-independent 'hallucination substrate'.

title: Web-caption frequency of a class name predicts its open-vocabulary dense performance better than annotation count, object size, or visual distinctiveness.
core_hypothesis: A frequency proxy for the class name in web captions is the single strongest predictor of per-class dense performance, dominating visual covariates in a joint regression, implying 'open vocabulary' quality is mostly 'frequent vocabulary' quality.

title: Reporting bias in captions creates a grounding gap for visually obvious but rarely mentioned attributes (wetness, material, temperature cues).
core_hypothesis: Attribute words with high visual detectability but low caption mention rate (because they are pragmatically obvious) will show disproportionately poor dense grounding compared to attributes matched for visual detectability but mentioned often.

title: Web captions are spatially impoverished, so scaling caption data improves noun grounding but not spatial-relation grounding, a divergence measurable on scaling families.
core_hypothesis: Because precise spatial constructions are rare and often wrong in alt-text, relation-grounding performance across a data-scaling family of VLMs will be nearly flat while noun grounding climbs, showing a supervision ceiling rather than a capacity ceiling.

title: Rare-class dense performance is text-side-bottlenecked: remapping rare names to frequent synonyms recovers most of the gap, capping out at the synonym's own performance.
core_hypothesis: For rare classes with a frequent near-synonym, substituting the frequent name recovers a large fraction of the performance gap without touching the vision side, and the recovered performance asymptotes at the frequent synonym's level, identifying the text tower as the binding constraint.

title: Homonym class names are grounded to their caption-dominant sense, and dense systems ignore disambiguating context supplied in the prompt.
core_hypothesis: Dense predictions for homonyms follow the corpus-dominant sense regardless of scene content, and appending disambiguating context shifts predictions only marginally because the head noun's embedding dominates the pooled query.

title: Proper nouns (brands, landmarks) are dense-grounded disproportionately well relative to matched common nouns, exposing alt-text memorization as a hidden performance component.
core_hypothesis: Dense grounding of proper nouns exceeds that of common nouns matched for visual specificity and frequency, because alt-text disproportionately names entities; this gap quantifies how much 'open-vocabulary' skill is retrieval-like memorization.

title: Compound class names activate on their component words: 'fire hydrant' queries produce spurious dense responses on fires and hydrant-unrelated red objects.
core_hypothesis: Patch-level responses to compound queries decompose approximately linearly into component-word responses, causing predictable false positives on component referents; the decomposition residual (compound minus components) predicts which compounds are safely usable in vocabularies.

title: Dense transfer of VLMs degrades sharply beyond the positional-embedding interpolation regime, and the bottleneck is PE handling, not feature quality.
core_hypothesis: Performance versus inference resolution is smooth within a moderate interpolation range and then deteriorates nonlinearly, and swapping PE-handling strategies (interpolation scheme, windowed attention, PE-free variants) at fixed weights moves the breakdown point, proving the bottleneck is positional, not representational.

title: Sliding-window inference for VLM dense prediction concentrates errors at window boundaries and systematically loses global-context-dependent classes.
core_hypothesis: Error density is elevated in a band around window borders, and classes whose recognition depends on global context (stuff classes, scene-dependent objects) lose disproportionate accuracy under windowing versus full-image inference at matched effective resolution.

title: Token merging and pruning methods benchmarked on VQA silently devastate dense prediction at the same token budgets.
core_hypothesis: At matched token-reduction ratios, dense metrics degrade several times faster than VQA metrics because merging preferentially destroys within-object boundary tokens that global tasks never needed; the degradation is predictable from merge-map geometry.

title: Multi-crop high-resolution schemes in LLM-based VLMs leave crop-seam inconsistencies detectable as grid-aligned artifacts in dense outputs.
core_hypothesis: Dense predictions from multi-crop VLMs show statistically elevated discontinuity along crop boundaries (label flips, depth jumps) relative to matched within-crop locations, and objects straddling seams suffer measurable accuracy penalties.

title: VLM features underweight high spatial frequencies, and boundary quality gains more from frequency-targeted feature surgery than from resolution increases at matched cost.
core_hypothesis: The frequency spectrum of VLM patch features is biased low relative to dense-supervised backbones, and injecting cheap high-frequency pathways (early-layer skips, edge-aware modulation) improves boundary F-score more per FLOP than resolution scaling.
mutation_note: Spectral-deficit measurement and the cost-matched boundary-vs-resolution comparison are the falsifiable content; 'inject early-layer skips / edge-aware modulation' is a module graft. Mutate: pathway becomes a validation instrument, not the contribution.

title: Textual coordinate outputs of VLMs quantize localization: error histograms carry the signature of the coordinate token vocabulary, not visual uncertainty.
core_hypothesis: Localization residuals cluster at the spacing implied by coordinate token granularity, and total error decomposes into a quantization floor plus a visual term; models with finer coordinate vocabularies show proportionally lower floors independent of visual backbone quality.

title: Decoding hyperparameters (temperature, top-p) change dense grounding metrics of LLM-based VLMs by margins comparable to model-choice differences, yet go unreported.
core_hypothesis: Localization and mask metrics vary substantially across reasonable decoding configurations, sometimes reordering model comparisons, meaning part of reported progress is decoding-configuration luck.

title: Predicted coordinates from VLMs spike at round numbers, inheriting digit-token priors from language pretraining and biasing localization.
core_hypothesis: Histograms of predicted coordinates show excess mass at round values (multiples of ten, powers of two) beyond what ground-truth distributions justify, and the bias magnitude predicts a recoverable localization error via post-hoc de-biasing.

title: Text-serialized mask formats accumulate error toward the end of the generation order, producing a bottom-right accuracy gradient that flips when the serialization order is reversed.
core_hypothesis: Autoregressive drift (context dilution, early-error conditioning) makes later-generated regions less accurate, creating a spatial accuracy gradient aligned with serialization order rather than image content; training with reversed or randomized order relocates the gradient accordingly.

title: The textual output format chosen for dense supervision (box corners versus center-size versus polygon) reshapes the model's internal spatial representation, not just its output accuracy.
core_hypothesis: Models finetuned with different output encodings develop measurably different internal spatial representations (probed for object extent, center, and adjacency), so format is a representational prior: center-size training improves center probing, corner training improves extent probing, beyond what output accuracy differences explain.

title: Chain-of-thought prompting improves VLM semantic answers but degrades pointing and dense localization on the same queries.
core_hypothesis: Interposed reasoning tokens dilute visual attention available at coordinate-emission time, so CoT trades semantic accuracy for localization accuracy; the localization drop correlates with reasoning-chain length.

title: Routing all mask information through a single special token (SEG-token architectures) caps multi-instance and fine-detail segmentation by an information bottleneck measurable in instance count.
core_hypothesis: A single token's hidden state cannot encode arbitrarily many instances or high-frequency detail, so accuracy will degrade with required instance count and contour complexity faster than for multi-token or per-query interfaces, and allocating more mask tokens will recover accuracy in proportion.

title: VLM-based monocular depth leans on recognized-object size priors and fails systematically on scenes with misleading familiar-size cues (miniatures, forced perspective).
core_hypothesis: Depth systems built on VLM features weight familiar-size priors heavily, so on miniature scenes, dioramas, and forced-perspective photography their error explodes in the direction the prior predicts, while geometry-first baselines degrade gracefully.

title: Text conditioning in language-conditioned depth and dense-geometry models is largely a no-op: ablating or shuffling the prompt barely changes outputs.
core_hypothesis: Because geometric supervision dominates training gradients, the text branch atrophies: prompt ablation, shuffling, or contradiction changes dense outputs by less than internal sampling noise, so the 'language-conditioned' label describes the architecture, not the function.

title: Depth decoded from VLM features is piecewise-constant per object: good at per-object median depth, poor at within-object depth gradients.
core_hypothesis: Semantic features support object-level depth assignment but lack surface-gradient information, so VLM-feature depth error decomposes into small between-object and large within-object components, the reverse of geometry-pretrained features.

title: VLM-derived depth relies on the vertical-position-in-image shortcut and breaks under camera roll and unusual viewpoints far more than geometric baselines.
core_hypothesis: Because caption-style pretraining and depth finetuning share upright-camera statistics, VLM-feature depth weights the y-coordinate cue heavily; rotating inputs degrades it disproportionately, and attribution analysis will show y-position dominance.

title: Scene-description prompts causally shift the metric scale of language-aware depth models, revealing exploitable and dangerous language-prior leakage.
core_hypothesis: Prompting a language-aware depth system with contradictory scene types ('a photo of a vast canyon' for an indoor scene) shifts predicted metric scale in the prior-consistent direction, showing that scale is partly read off language rather than pixels.

title: VLM-feature depth quality drops on unrecognized objects even when their geometry is trivially simple, demonstrating category-mediated rather than geometric depth computation.
core_hypothesis: Per-object depth error of VLM-feature models correlates with recognition confidence rather than shape complexity: simple unfamiliar shapes (blank boxes, abstract forms) receive worse depth than complex familiar objects at matched size and placement.

title: Spatial-QA competence and dense-geometry competence dissociate across VLM systems: models answer 'which is closer' correctly while their dense depth is wrong, and vice versa.
core_hypothesis: QA and dense geometry draw on partially disjoint mechanisms (verbal priors and object statistics versus per-pixel evidence), so across a model population the two scores correlate weakly, and per-image agreement between the QA answer and the model's own dense output is far from perfect, exposing internal inconsistency.

title: Metric-scale accuracy of VLM-era depth models depends on incidental scale metadata correlations (scene type, camera signature) and collapses to relative depth when those cues are randomized.
core_hypothesis: Models infer scale from dataset-correlated cues (indoor/outdoor type, lens rendering, typical object sets) rather than from geometry; on images where such cues are neutralized or set into conflict, metric error inflates dramatically while relative (ordinal) accuracy is preserved.

title: Base/novel splits in open-vocabulary benchmarks leak through web pretraining: 'novel' classes are often pretraining-frequent, so benchmarks measure vocabulary recall, not generalization.
core_hypothesis: Performance on 'novel' classes is strongly stratified by their pretraining-frequency proxy, and the subset of genuinely rare novel classes shows a dramatically larger base-novel gap, meaning headline open-vocabulary gains concentrate on pseudo-novel classes.

title: String-matched class scoring in open-vocabulary evaluation penalizes correct predictions under alternative names, and the automatic-versus-human evaluation gap grows with vocabulary openness.
core_hypothesis: A human-judged or embedding-similarity-judged re-scoring of open-vocabulary dense predictions will recover substantial performance relative to exact-match scoring, and the recovery will differ across methods, changing some rankings, because methods differ in name-choice behavior rather than grounding quality.

title: Decomposing referring-segmentation error into grounding (wrong object) versus delineation (right object, bad mask) reorders model rankings and reveals divergent failure profiles.
core_hypothesis: Models differ qualitatively in their grounding-versus-delineation error mix at similar aggregate IoU, so component-wise evaluation changes rankings and shows that some celebrated architectures win only one component.

title: Cross-paper comparisons of open-vocabulary segmentation are dominated by inconsistent background/ignore-label conventions rather than method differences.
core_hypothesis: Re-evaluating several published methods under one unified convention will compress or reorder reported differences, showing that convention variance is comparable to claimed method improvements in this literature.

title: Per-benchmark prompt curation is unacknowledged test-set tuning: standardized frozen prompt protocols would materially reorder open-vocabulary dense leaderboards.
core_hypothesis: A frozen, shared prompt protocol (fixed templates, fixed names, no per-benchmark curation) will change method rankings, and the methods that drop most will be those whose ablations attribute the least gain to architecture.

title: Adding verified-absent 'negative vocabulary' queries to open-vocabulary dense evaluation reorders models by exposing hallucination costs that standard AP never charges.
core_hypothesis: Models differ widely in absent-query false-positive behavior at matched present-query accuracy, so a combined metric charging for negative-query responses will separate models that current benchmarks call equivalent and demote some leaders.

title: Per-pixel confidence from VLM segmenters is miscalibrated in a class- and region-structured way that no single temperature can fix.
core_hypothesis: Calibration error varies systematically with class frequency, region type (boundary versus interior), and query-set composition, so global temperature scaling leaves large conditional miscalibration; a structured calibrator (per-frequency-tier, distance-to-boundary-aware) removes most of it.

title: Spatial autocorrelation of dense-prediction errors breaks the effective-sample-size assumptions of conformal and risk-control methods applied per pixel.
core_hypothesis: The spatial correlation length of VLM segmentation errors is large enough that nominal per-pixel guarantees are badly miscovered at the image and region level; correcting with measured effective sample sizes restores advertised coverage at the cost of wider sets.

title: Variance across prompt paraphrases is a stronger per-pixel error predictor for VLM dense prediction than standard confidence or MC dropout.
core_hypothesis: Because dense errors are often driven by query-embedding fragility, the pixel-wise variance of predictions across meaning-preserving paraphrases identifies error-prone regions better than logit confidence or dropout variance, at a handful of extra inference passes.

title: Abstention thresholds for open-vocabulary dense prediction do not transfer across query vocabularies, making per-vocabulary recalibration a hidden deployment requirement.
core_hypothesis: Similarity-score distributions shift with vocabulary size and composition (via normalization and competition effects), so a threshold tuned on one vocabulary yields wildly different precision-recall operating points on another; the shift is predictable from vocabulary statistics, enabling analytic threshold correction.

title: In LLM-based segmenters, verbalized uncertainty and mask confidence are uncorrelated: the model 'says' it is unsure while emitting high-confidence masks, and vice versa.
core_hypothesis: Verbalized confidence (elicited via standard prompts) and mask-head confidence are computed by weakly coupled mechanisms, so their correlation across examples is low and neither dominates as an error predictor; their disagreement itself is an informative error flag.

title: Distance of a query embedding from the pretraining caption manifold predicts per-query dense reliability, giving a deployment-time reliability score with no labels.
core_hypothesis: Queries embedding far from the density of pretraining-like caption embeddings (approximated by a public caption corpus) receive systematically worse dense performance, and this text-side distance is a stronger reliability predictor than query length, frequency, or visual difficulty proxies.

title: Dense finetuning collapses open-vocabulary alignment early and abruptly rather than gradually, and the collapse is detectable within the first fraction of training.
core_hypothesis: Vocabulary breadth (zero-shot performance on held-out class sets) drops in a sharp early phase tied to large initial gradient norms, not smoothly over training, so cheap interventions targeted at the first phase (warmup, text-tower freezing, gradient clipping) preserve most breadth at no dense-accuracy cost.

title: Adapting only the text tower recovers most of dense-adaptation gains, indicating vision features are already dense-sufficient and the mismatch lives on the language side.
core_hypothesis: At matched trainable-parameter budgets, text-side-only adaptation (query embeddings, text adapters) achieves a large fraction of the improvement of vision-side adaptation for open-vocabulary dense tasks, because the binding constraint is aligning queries to already-present visual structure.

title: Conclusions that VLMs 'lack localization ability' are probe artifacts: nonparametric decoders extract far more spatial information from frozen features than the linear probes used to write off the models.
core_hypothesis: Dense information in VLM features is present but non-linearly and non-locally coded, so retrieval-based and attention-readout decoders reveal substantially better localization than linear probes at matched supervision, changing several published capability conclusions.

title: Weight-space interpolation between a pretrained VLM and its dense-finetuned child traces a better breadth-versus-density tradeoff than joint multi-task training.
core_hypothesis: The pretrained and dense-finetuned weights are linearly connected with low loss barriers for both objectives, so post-hoc interpolation offers a free family of tradeoff models, some strictly dominating jointly trained baselines on the breadth-density Pareto front.

title: Dense adaptation has a qualitatively higher LoRA-rank floor than classification adaptation, revealing that dense transfer is not a low-intrinsic-dimension update.
core_hypothesis: The intrinsic dimensionality of the update needed for dense tasks (which must alter spatial feature structure, not just class boundaries) is fundamentally higher, so dense accuracy saturates at much higher ranks and low-rank runs silently sacrifice boundary quality first.

title: Distilling a VLM into a dense specialist preserves open-vocabulary breadth better than finetuning the VLM itself, at matched dense accuracy.
core_hypothesis: Keeping the VLM frozen as a teacher and distilling its patch-text affinities into a student dense architecture avoids touching the alignment that finetuning damages, yielding a better breadth-density operating point than direct finetuning at matched compute.

title: Paraphrase robustness collapses before seen-prompt accuracy during dense finetuning, providing an early-warning metric for alignment damage.
core_hypothesis: Finetuning first destroys the text encoder's local semantic smoothness: performance under paraphrased prompts diverges from canonical-prompt performance well before canonical-prompt metrics move, so paraphrase-gap tracking predicts eventual breadth loss early enough to intervene.

title: Attribute-object binding fails at pixel level in predictable directions: dense models swap attributes between instances rather than failing randomly.
core_hypothesis: When multiple attribute-bearing instances are present, dense predictions exhibit structured swaps (attributes migrate to the more salient or larger instance) rather than uniform noise, and swap direction is predicted by a saliency-asymmetry score computable from the image alone.

title: Attribute information in VLM features is channel-sparse: a few feature directions carry color/material/state, and causal edits to them flip dense predictions.
core_hypothesis: Linear attribute directions identified on patch features generalize across categories and positions, and intervening on them (projection removal, direction addition) changes attribute-conditioned dense predictions in the predicted direction without disturbing category predictions, demonstrating sparse, manipulable attribute coding.

title: Part-whole queries fail asymmetrically: 'the wheel of the car' returns whole-car masks, and part grounding quality is predicted by the part's caption-mention rate, not its visual size.
core_hypothesis: Dense predictions for part queries are biased toward the containing whole, with the bias strength inversely related to how often the part is independently captioned in web text; frequently captioned parts (face, wheel) ground well while rarely captioned parts (hinge, cuff) collapse to wholes.

title: Training with programmatically recombined captions improves pixel-level binding but measurably degrades rare-noun grounding, a compositionality-versus-coverage tradeoff nobody reports.
core_hypothesis: Recombined captions inject distributional noise for rare nouns (attaching them to atypical contexts), so binding gains come with a hidden tax on rare-vocabulary dense performance; the tradeoff is tunable by restricting recombination to frequent nouns.

title: A dense analogue of minimal-pair compositional benchmarks will show VLM dense systems near chance on composition even when their global image-text matching succeeds.
core_hypothesis: On minimal pairs distinguishable only by composition (same objects and attributes, different binding or relation), dense systems will assign masks at near-chance consistency with the intended reading, and their dense compositional score will be uncorrelated with their retrieval-level compositional score, showing the two abilities dissociate.

title: Non-English prompts degrade dense prediction disproportionately relative to classification, because pixel-level matching amplifies text-embedding quality differences.
core_hypothesis: Dense tasks compound per-query embedding error across thousands of pixel decisions, so the multilingual performance gap (relative to English) will be systematically larger for segmentation/detection than for classification on matched concepts, and largest for low-resource languages.

title: For non-photographic imagery (thermal, ultrasound, sketches), VLM dense failure is vision-encoder-side, not text-side, and the attribution is measurable by asymmetric substitution.
core_hypothesis: Substituting a modality-adapted vision encoder (while keeping original text queries) recovers far more dense performance than any text-side intervention (rewriting, ensembling) on the frozen original encoder, establishing that the modality gap lives almost entirely in vision feature extraction.

title: Open-vocabulary dense performance varies geographically for the same class, tracking the geographic distribution of captioned imagery rather than visual difficulty.
core_hypothesis: Per-region dense performance for common classes correlates with estimated regional representation in caption corpora, after controlling for image quality and scene clutter, revealing a geographic fairness gap specific to the open-vocabulary mechanism.

title: In unfamiliar visual domains, VLM dense grounding falls back to texture words over shape words, re-expressing the texture bias at the language-grounding level.
core_hypothesis: Out of distribution, queries built from texture and material words will localize regions substantially better than queries built from shape words, mirroring the classic texture bias but now measurable through the language interface, and implying that OOD vocabulary design should prefer material descriptions.

title: Code-switched prompts (mixed-language queries) break dense grounding disproportionately, exposing tokenizer-level fragility invisible in single-language evaluations.
core_hypothesis: Code-switching fragments tokenization and pushes query embeddings off both languages' manifolds, so dense performance under code-switched prompts falls below the worse of the two single-language conditions, rather than between them as a smooth-interpolation view would predict.

title: Referring-segmentation benchmarks are largely solvable from the head noun plus saliency, so modifier-ablated evaluation is needed to measure actual referring ability.
core_hypothesis: Ablating all modifiers from referring expressions (keeping only the head noun) preserves the large majority of benchmark accuracy for top systems, meaning the benchmarks mostly test open-vocabulary object detection, and true referring skill is concentrated in (and measurable on) the small expression subset where ablation hurts.

title: Correction turns ('no, the other one') fail in dense VLM systems because nothing represents the rejected hypothesis, and a minimal exclusion memory fixes a large fraction of failures.
core_hypothesis: On correction turns, current systems re-predict their first choice at high rates (having no representation of 'not that one'), and augmenting inference with an explicit exclusion constraint (suppress the previously returned instance) recovers most correction-turn failures without retraining.
