title: Beyond their information content, longer referring expressions actively hurt dense grounding: added words dilute attention rather than adding constraints.
core_hypothesis: For a fixed referent and fixed disambiguating information, padding expressions with redundant true details reduces grounding accuracy monotonically, because pooled or cross-attended text representations dilute the discriminative tokens; the effect is stronger in contrastive-tower systems than LLM-decoder systems.

title: Detection recall for small objects drops as a step function of object size measured in patches, not a smooth function of size in pixels, creating hidden size cliffs set by preprocessing policy.
core_hypothesis: Per-object failure probability in transformer detectors has discontinuities at integer patch-count boundaries (especially below roughly 2x2 patches), so the operative variable is patches-per-object, and resize policy is a hidden failure knob.

title: Fixed-square-input models fail disproportionately on objects whose apparent aspect ratio is inverted or extremized by anisotropic resize of extreme-aspect images (panoramas, documents, strips).
core_hypothesis: Failure probability on extreme-aspect images is predicted primarily by the per-object deformation factor introduced by the resize, and is largely removed by aspect-preserving tiling, showing the failure is a preprocessing geometry artifact.

title: When ViTs run at resolutions unseen in training, positional-embedding interpolation concentrates errors in specific spatial zones (borders and corners) independent of image content.
core_hypothesis: Dense-prediction error at transfer resolutions has a content-independent spatial signature determined by the positional embedding interpolation scheme, with error mass concentrated where interpolation distortion is largest.

title: High-norm artifact/register tokens in DINO-family backbones spatially co-locate with a specific class of downstream segmentation leaks into textureless background.
core_hypothesis: Patches hosting artifact tokens carry corrupted local features, so downstream segmentation heads systematically leak masks into (or hallucinate structure within) the textureless regions where artifact tokens preferentially appear.

title: Thin-structure segmentation failure is governed by the structure's orientation relative to the sampling grid (aliasing angle), not primarily by its width.
core_hypothesis: For fixed physical width, per-pixel recall on thin structures is a periodic function of orientation angle modulo 90 degrees, with minima at angles of maximal aliasing, and this angle effect exceeds the width effect over a practically relevant range.

title: Windowed-attention backbones (Swin-like) localize object boundaries systematically worse when those boundaries coincide with attention-window seams.
core_hypothesis: Boundary localization error is elevated in a band around window seams, and the elevation persists (attenuated) through shifted-window schemes, making window geometry a content-independent predictor of where a model fails.

title: Vision models trained on web-scale data treat JPEG compression artifacts as part of natural image statistics, so pristine uncompressed imagery (medical, RAW, professional) is out-of-distribution and fails in characteristic ways.
core_hypothesis: Model features partially entrain on block-DCT artifact statistics; on artifact-free images, texture-dependent predictions shift systematically, and lightly re-compressing pristine images toward the training distribution's typical quality improves accuracy.

title: Silent mismatches between train-time and inference-time resize interpolation kernels (bilinear vs bicubic vs area, antialias flags) cause reproducible small-object and texture failures that get misattributed to domain shift.
core_hypothesis: A measurable fraction of reported cross-deployment accuracy variance for the same checkpoint is caused by interpolation-kernel mismatch, with damage concentrated in high-frequency content (small objects, textures, thin edges).

title: A measurable share of mined 'model failures' are actually silent metadata mishandling (EXIF rotation, embedded ICC color profiles) upstream of the model, contaminating failure taxonomies.
core_hypothesis: Auditing mined failure sets for metadata-handling divergence between the serving pipeline and the review pipeline will reclaim a nontrivial fraction of cases as pipeline artifacts, and this fraction is systematically higher for mobile-captured imagery.

title: Vision models silently assume sRGB; wide-gamut and HDR content gets clipped or misencoded at ingestion, producing hue-specific failures concentrated in highly saturated regions.
core_hypothesis: Predictions on objects whose identity depends on saturated color (produce ripeness, signage, safety markings, skin tones under saturated lighting) degrade systematically for wide-gamut sources, with error concentrated in pixels outside the sRGB gamut.

title: Legacy ImageNet normalization constants bias modern models at luminance extremes: systematic failure concentration in very dark and very bright images that tracks the mismatch between corpus statistics and hardcoded mean/std.
core_hypothesis: Error rates conditioned on image luminance percentile rise disproportionately at the tails, and part of that rise is attributable to normalization mismatch rather than information loss, since re-calibrating normalization to the deployment corpus reduces tail error without retraining the backbone.

title: Segmenters trained on composited product/stock imagery learn 'uniform white equals background,' causing systematic failure on genuinely white or high-key objects and scenes.
core_hypothesis: Foreground/background decisions near uniform bright regions are driven partly by the compositing shortcut, so white objects on white scenes (snow, lab equipment, linens, appliances) suffer characteristic mask erosion that vanishes when the same shapes are recolored.

title: Frames extracted from compressed video (chroma subsampling, deinterlacing, keyframe artifacts) form a distinct sub-domain in training corpora, and models inherit failure modes tied to those artifacts' presence or absence.
core_hypothesis: Models learn partially separate processing regimes for video-artifact and photographic content, so color-boundary-critical predictions (small colored objects, chroma-defined edges) degrade on whichever side is rarer in training, and artifact-matched preprocessing shifts accuracy predictably.

title: Most web images carry a downscale-then-upscale resampling signature; models partially key on it, and 'native-resolution' imagery (direct camera capture) is subtly out-of-distribution.
core_hypothesis: Model accuracy has a component predicted by the resampling-history signature of the input, so native captures fail at elevated rates on texture- and sharpness-sensitive predictions, and imposing a web-typical resample chain on native captures recovers accuracy.

title: Segmenters reproduce dataset-specific annotator boundary conventions (systematic inset/outset of polygons), so cross-dataset boundary scores measure convention mismatch rather than localization competence.
core_hypothesis: Each training corpus induces a signed, roughly constant boundary offset in model predictions; cross-dataset boundary F-score differences are dominated by offset mismatch, and removing a fitted global offset collapses much of the apparent cross-dataset boundary gap.

title: Models trained on mixtures of amodal and modal annotation policies blend the two, producing occlusion-boundary predictions that follow neither policy and fail predictably in proportion to the training mixture.
core_hypothesis: Under occlusion, predicted mask extent interpolates between modal and amodal conventions with a mixing coefficient determined by training data proportions, so occlusion errors are policy-blend artifacts rather than perception failures, and are predictable without looking at the image content.

title: COCO-style 'crowd/ignore' regions teach detectors to suppress predictions in high-density areas, so recall collapse in dense scenes is partly a trained suppression behavior, not a capacity limit.
core_hypothesis: Detectors trained with crowd-ignore conventions internalize density-conditioned suppression: at matched per-instance visibility, recall drops as local instance density rises, and models trained on fully-instance-annotated dense data of the same scenes do not show the same drop.

title: Stock-photo watermarks and text overlays correlated with specific classes act as hidden features; a measurable slice of class-conditional accuracy evaporates when watermarks are removed or transplanted.
core_hypothesis: For classes whose training imagery is watermark-enriched, model confidence and accuracy depend partly on watermark presence, so cleaned images lose accuracy and watermark-transplanted negatives gain false positives, with effect size predictable from per-class watermark prevalence in the corpus.

title: Detector and VLM object hallucination rates follow a quantitative law driven by class co-occurrence statistics of training corpora: hallucinated objects are those whose contextual partners are present.
core_hypothesis: The probability that a model hallucinates class B in an image containing class A is an increasing, approximately monotone function of the corpus co-occurrence P(B|A), so hallucination is predictable scene-by-scene from corpus statistics alone, before running the model.

title: Photographer framing bias makes object-position-in-frame a learned prior: recognition and detection degrade with distance from typical framing positions, and each corpus leaves a measurable positional fingerprint in its models.
core_hypothesis: Per-object failure probability as a function of normalized image position forms a stable, model-specific surface (the positional fingerprint) that (a) mirrors the training corpus's object-position density and (b) transfers across content categories, so peripheral placements fail at rates unexplained by resolution or lens distortion.

title: Vertex-budget limits of polygon annotation tools cap the boundary curvature present in ground truth, so segmenters inherit a curvature ceiling: they cannot produce high-curvature boundaries even when image evidence supports them.
core_hypothesis: The curvature spectrum of model-predicted boundaries is bounded by the curvature spectrum of training annotations rather than by image evidence, so models systematically round corners and serrations, and training on curvature-rich synthetic supervision lifts the ceiling without architecture changes.

title: Ground-truth false negatives (unannotated real objects) train detectors into category-specific under-detection, so part of what benchmarks call 'hard categories' is annotation incompleteness echoed by the model.
core_hypothesis: Per-category deployed recall is depressed in proportion to the category's ground-truth miss rate in training data, and re-scoring benchmarks with exhaustively re-annotated ground truth reorders both category difficulty rankings and model rankings.

title: Near-duplicate leakage between web-scale pretraining data and evaluation sets deflates measured failure rates: deduplicated evaluations reveal a hidden mass of failures and change robustness conclusions.
core_hypothesis: Stratifying evaluation by pretraining-similarity (embedding-space nearest-neighbor distance to the training corpus) will show failure rates rising steeply in the far-from-corpus stratum, and headline robustness claims shrink materially when only the uncontaminated stratum is scored.

title: VLM failure on visual concepts tracks the linguistic provenance of training captions: concepts described mostly in particular languages or caption styles fail when queried outside that provenance.
core_hypothesis: Per-concept VLM accuracy is predicted by the caption-language and phrasing distribution under which that concept appears in training, so translating the query toward the dominant training phrasing recovers accuracy, revealing that many 'visual' failures are provenance mismatches.

title: Failures of independently developed vision FMs are highly correlated because of shared web data, imposing a hard ceiling on ensemble and cross-check safety architectures.
core_hypothesis: Across model families with different architectures and training recipes, per-image failure indicators exhibit correlation well above what accuracy levels alone imply, and the shared-failure core is enriched in data-borne causes (rare compositions, convention conflicts) rather than architecture-specific ones.

title: Distillation and fine-tuning transmit failure sets nearly intact along model lineages, making failure provenance traceable like a phylogeny across the model ecosystem.
core_hypothesis: Per-instance failure overlap between teacher and student is far higher than accuracy-matched unrelated pairs, persists through multiple derivation generations with a measurable decay rate, and is strong enough that failure fingerprints alone can identify a model's ancestor among candidates.

title: Per-image failure persistence across model generations is bimodal: transient failures that any scale increase fixes, and permanent failures immune to generation changes, with different causal signatures.
core_hypothesis: Tracking fixed evaluation instances across a model lineage will show failure lifetimes clustering into two modes (fixed at the next generation versus never fixed), the permanent mode being enriched in label-convention conflicts, adjudication-ambiguous content, and information-theoretically limited inputs rather than capability gaps.

title: Test-time augmentation agreement is higher on failures than successes for shortcut-driven errors: models are consistently wrong under augmentation exactly where TTA-disagreement detectors are trusted to fire.
core_hypothesis: Failure cases split by augmentation-consistency: ambiguity failures show low TTA agreement while shortcut and prior-driven failures show TTA agreement as high as correct predictions, so TTA-based failure detection has a structural blind spot covering the most dangerous (confident, systematic) errors.

title: Naturally-occurring failure images and adversarial perturbation directions share low-dimensional subspace structure, so mining natural failures can substitute for expensive adversarial search and vice versa.
core_hypothesis: Feature-space directions that separate natural failure cases from matched successes align significantly with locally-computed adversarial gradient directions, implying a shared vulnerability subspace, so hardening against mined natural failures transfers to adversarial robustness within that subspace and vice versa.

title: Ecosystem-wide reliance on a few frozen backbones (CLIP, DINO) creates feature-level correlated blind spots: inputs poorly separated in backbone feature space fail across all downstream heads simultaneously.
core_hypothesis: There exist characterizable input regions where backbone feature geometry collapses distinctions (feature-space confusability), and downstream failure across independent heads is predicted by that confusability score computed from the backbone alone, defining a systemic-risk map independent of any head.

title: The natural failure set of a vision FM concentrates in a low-rank feature subspace: a handful of 'failure directions' explains most failure mass, making failures compressible and monitorable.
core_hypothesis: Displacements between failures and matched successes in FM feature space are low-rank: a small number of directions captures a large share of failure variance, the directions are semantically interpretable (e.g., lighting regimes, style axes), and distance along them predicts failure probability on fresh data.

title: Model errors form two mechanistically distinct populations, confidently-wrong (shortcut/prior-driven) and diffidently-wrong (ambiguity-driven), and every mitigation helps one while leaving or harming the other.
core_hypothesis: The error population of vision FMs is bimodal in confidence and in cause: high-confidence errors trace to shortcuts and priors while low-confidence errors trace to genuine ambiguity, and standard mitigations (temperature scaling, selective prediction, TTA) exclusively address the low-confidence mode, leaving the high-confidence mode as an invariant residual.

title: Per-pixel segmentation confidence is spatially anti-aligned with error severity: lowest at tolerable boundary zones, highest inside regions where errors are catastrophic whole-instance mistakes.
core_hypothesis: The spatial distribution of segmentation confidence is dominated by boundary proximity rather than semantic risk, so severity-weighted risk (probability times cost of the error at that pixel) is anti-correlated with the confidence map's implied risk over a large fraction of images, making confidence maps actively misleading for downstream risk consumers.

title: Classification confidence and localization quality of detections are nearly statistically independent, so score-threshold failure mining systematically misses the well-scored badly-localized failure stratum.
core_hypothesis: Across detector families, the mutual information between classification score and localization error (IoU with truth) is low, so a distinct failure stratum exists (high score, poor box) that score-based mining never samples, and this stratum is enriched in downstream-harmful cases (truncated boxes on pedestrians, merged boxes on adjacent objects).

title: Calibration transfers across class-prior shift in a predictable direction: models calibrated on balanced sets become overconfident on majority classes and underconfident on minority classes in deployment, with error computable from the prior ratio alone.
core_hypothesis: For softmax classifiers, deployment miscalibration under pure prior shift follows the analytic Bayes correction determined by the train-to-deploy prior ratio, so measured deployment calibration error will match the closed-form prediction, and applying the correction restores calibration without new labeled data beyond prior estimates.

title: Under style shift (paintings, sketches, renders), model confidence does not degrade smoothly but bifurcates toward extremes, invalidating threshold-based OOD triggers precisely on stylized inputs.
core_hypothesis: As inputs move along a photo-to-abstract style continuum, per-input confidence distributions transition from unimodal to bimodal (near-one and near-zero lobes) rather than shifting downward, so any single confidence threshold either floods alerts or misses the confident-wrong lobe entirely.

title: SAM-style mask quality scores inherit the prompt distribution of training: quality prediction fails specifically for atypical prompts (boundary-adjacent, off-center, multi-point), mis-ranking masks exactly when users prompt unusually.
core_hypothesis: Quality-score reliability (correlation with true IoU) degrades sharply as prompts depart from the training prompt distribution, so for boundary-adjacent or unusually-placed prompts the model both segments worse and mis-scores its candidates, compounding failure at selection time.

title: A single temperature calibrated in-domain moves calibration in a predictable harmful direction under covariate shift (overconfidence grows with feature-space shift distance), making shift distance a sufficient statistic for recalibration.
core_hypothesis: Calibration error under covariate shift grows monotonically with feature-space distance from the calibration set, always in the overconfident direction for in-domain-calibrated models, so a distance-conditioned temperature (one scalar function, no shift labels) restores most calibration across shifts.

title: VLMs switch from vision to language-prior answering at a measurable visual-evidence threshold: a psychometric 'blindness point' that is a stable model constant across content.
core_hypothesis: For questions with prior-consistent and prior-violating answers, VLM accuracy as a function of visual evidence strength (contrast, size, occlusion of the deciding cue) follows a psychometric curve whose inflection (the blindness point) is stable across content domains for a given model, making prior-override behavior predictable from one calibration set.

title: VLM counting errors mirror human numerosity psychophysics (exact subitizing up to about four, logarithmic error growth beyond) because caption statistics encode human number usage, not because models perceive numerosity.
core_hypothesis: VLM count-response distributions will show human-like signatures: near-perfect small-number performance, scalar variability (error proportional to magnitude), and round-number attraction, and these signatures will track caption corpus number-word frequencies rather than image encoder capacity, implying counting is linguistic prior readout above the subitizing range.

title: Left/right spatial-relation failures in VLMs are chiral: systematically asymmetric in a direction matching reading-order statistics of training captions, so mirroring images flips the error asymmetry.
core_hypothesis: VLMs answer 'A left of B' questions with an asymmetric error profile (one direction systematically overreported), the asymmetry sign matches subject-first/reading-order biases in caption corpora, and horizontally mirroring the entire evaluation flips the model's error asymmetry, proving the bias is representational rather than stimulus-driven.

title: Open-vocabulary detectors and VLMs match negated queries ('a cup without a handle') to the negated concept itself, and the failure is diagnosable entirely from the text encoder's geometry before any image is seen.
core_hypothesis: For contrastive text encoders, embeddings of negated attribute phrases are dominated by the negated content word, so text-side similarity structure alone (negated phrase near affirmative phrase) predicts image-side failure rates per concept, and text-encoder-only audits can forecast which negation queries a deployment will get wrong without any image evaluation.

title: Attribute-object binding errors in VLMs grow superlinearly with the number of attributed objects in the scene, following a capacity law of cross-attention rather than a per-object constant error rate.
core_hypothesis: Binding error per object rises with object count following a superlinear curve with a model-specific capacity knee, because attention resources for maintaining object-attribute association are shared and contended, so scene complexity is a quantitative predictor of binding failure and the knee is a comparable model constant.

title: Increasing input resolution without increasing visual token budget raises VLM hallucination on fine details: per-token information compression, not resolution, is the operative variable for detail fidelity.
core_hypothesis: Hallucination rate on detail-level questions is governed by pixels-per-visual-token rather than raw resolution, so raising resolution at fixed tokens increases detail hallucination in describable-but-compressed regions, while raising tokens at fixed resolution decreases it, making the compression ratio a design law for VLM configuration.

title: VLMs lean on embedded text as a crutch for perception questions: removing or altering incidental text in images collapses accuracy on questions that ostensibly require only visual understanding.
core_hypothesis: For a substantial fraction of benchmark items labeled as visual perception, model accuracy drops sharply when embedded text is inpainted away or adversarially altered, and the text-reliance fraction varies by capability category, being highest for fine-grained recognition and scene understanding, revealing inflated capability estimates.

title: VLM performance on an image is predicted by how likely that image's natural description is under web caption style: content whose honest description diverges from alt-text conventions fails regardless of visual difficulty.
core_hypothesis: The likelihood of an image's ground-truth description under a caption-style language model predicts VLM task accuracy on that image beyond visual difficulty measures, so style-improbable content (dashcam geometry, instrument panels, tables of objects) forms a coherent failure stratum invisible to visual-attribute mining.

title: VLM visual verification has a phrasing-dependent yes-bias: agreement rates track question-form frequency in training text, so the same visual fact gets different answers under logically equivalent phrasings.
core_hypothesis: For fixed visual evidence, the yes/no response distribution shifts systematically across logically equivalent phrasings (positive, negative, tag-question, existential forms), the shift direction follows form-frequency statistics of instruction corpora, and phrasing-marginalized evaluation changes both absolute scores and model rankings on standard verification suites.

title: Visual sycophancy is dose-dependent: VLM agreement with false user assertions about an image rises lawfully with the assertion's expressed confidence, quantifying how much visual evidence is worth against social pressure.
core_hypothesis: Agreement probability with a false visual claim is a smooth increasing function of linguistic assertion strength and a decreasing function of visual evidence strength, and the two combine in a stable, model-specific exchange rate (how much evidence offsets one step of assertiveness), which characterizes deployment risk better than any single sycophancy score.

title: VLMs read chart values by interpolating tick labels rather than measuring geometry: continuous-value readout errors quantize toward tick values and gridline positions, revealing symbolic rather than metric chart perception.
core_hypothesis: The error distribution of VLM continuous-value chart readouts concentrates at tick and gridline values (quantization), error magnitude scales with inter-tick spacing rather than rendering resolution, and removing tick labels collapses performance to near-chance even when geometry remains fully informative.

title: Multi-image VLM prompts exhibit serial-position failure: evidence in middle images is used less than in first or last positions, independent of content, mirroring long-context positional biases in the visual channel.
core_hypothesis: For questions answerable from exactly one of n images, accuracy as a function of the evidence image's position will be U-shaped (primacy and recency advantages), the effect will grow with n and with per-image token count, and position randomization will change measured multi-image capability scores for current benchmarks.

title: Viewpoint failure maps of detectors and VLMs are predictable from web pose statistics: performance tracks the rendering-estimated frequency of each viewpoint in web imagery, enabling failure forecasting without pose-labeled data.
core_hypothesis: Per-viewpoint accuracy for a category is an increasing function of that viewpoint's frequency in web imagery (estimable via pose estimation or rendering-based retrieval), the function's shape is shared across categories within a model, and therefore viewpoint failure maps for unseen categories are predictable from corpus statistics alone.

title: A large share of missed detections in crowded scenes are suppression failures, not recognition failures: the correct box existed before NMS or query deduplication and was deleted by the post-processing stage.
core_hypothesis: Auditing pre-suppression candidate sets will show that for crowded-scene misses, a well-localized correctly-classified candidate existed above a reasonable score in a substantial fraction of cases, so the operative failure is deduplication policy, and this fraction is architecture-dependent (highest for classical NMS, present but different for set-prediction deduplication).

title: DETR-style object queries specialize to spatial-scale niches during training, so scenes whose object layout mismatches the learned query portfolio fail predictably, computable from layout statistics without image content.
core_hypothesis: The per-scene miss rate of set-prediction detectors is predicted by a mismatch score between the scene's object layout distribution and the model's query specialization map (estimable offline from decoder cross-attention statistics), with overloaded niches producing misses even at low total object counts.

title: Fixed score thresholds do not transfer across domains: per-domain optimal thresholds vary enough to reorder failure importance, so much of mined deployed 'failure' is threshold miscalibration rather than model error.
core_hypothesis: Score distributions shift across deployment domains substantially more than ranking quality degrades, so per-domain threshold recalibration (no retraining) recovers a large fraction of apparent cross-domain failure, and mined failure sets before versus after recalibration differ enough to change remediation priorities.

title: Detection recall has cliffs at the aspect-ratio boundaries of learned box priors: elongated objects fail not gradually but at sharp prior-set boundaries that differ per architecture and are invisible in category-level metrics.
core_hypothesis: Per-object recall as a function of ground-truth box aspect ratio shows steep declines at architecture-specific boundary values traceable to prior sets (anchor ratios, query statistics, regression target normalization), so extreme-shape failures (ladders, poles, trains head-on, cables) are structured cliffs, and the cliff locations are predictable from the architecture configuration without any evaluation.

title: Recall for adjacent object pairs collapses at an architecture-specific inter-object IoU threshold: the collapse point is a signature of the deduplication mechanism (NMS versus set prediction), not of the data.
core_hypothesis: Plotting pair-recall (both objects found) against inter-object box IoU yields a sigmoid collapse whose midpoint and slope are stable per architecture family across datasets, with NMS-based models collapsing at their suppression threshold and set-prediction models collapsing later but more steeply, making the curve a fingerprint of deduplication logic measurable from behavior alone.

title: For out-of-vocabulary objects, class-agnostic localization survives while classification collapses: most 'unknown object' failures are label-space failures, and mining should separate the two channels.
core_hypothesis: On categories absent from training vocabularies, objectness and localization quality of modern detectors degrade mildly while classification fails near-totally, so channel-separated failure accounting will reattribute the majority of open-world misses from perception to labeling, and downstream mitigations (label-space expansion, retrieval-based naming) will recover much of the loss without touching the visual pathway.

title: Objects touching image borders are missed at rates far exceeding occlusion-matched interior objects because crop augmentation teaches 'truncated equals ignorable': a training-policy failure masquerading as an occlusion problem.
core_hypothesis: Detection recall conditioned on border contact will show a penalty beyond visibility-matched interior occlusion, the penalty size will vary with the training stack's crop-labeling policy (label-drop thresholds), and retraining with truncation-preserving labeling will shrink the border penalty without affecting interior performance.

title: Topology errors (fragmentation, false merges) in segmentation are invisible to IoU at the sizes that matter, so failure mining ranked by IoU systematically excludes the failure class that breaks downstream connectivity-dependent applications.
core_hypothesis: The correlation between IoU and topology correctness (Betti number errors, connectivity of skeletons) approaches zero for thin-structure content, so IoU-ranked failure mining recovers only a small fraction of topology failures, and topology-aware mining surfaces a disjoint, application-critical failure set with different visual causes (low-contrast gaps, crossings, junctions).

title: SAM-style part-whole granularity choice is intrinsically unstable: trivially small input perturbations flip the same prompt between part and whole masks, and the instability is a fixed property of ambiguity handling, not resolvable by prompt engineering.
core_hypothesis: For prompts near part-whole ambiguity, the selected-mask granularity flips under perturbations far below perceptual relevance, flip probability is predicted by the score margin between candidate masks, and no prompt-side strategy (offsets, multi-point) eliminates the unstable region because it reflects a decision boundary intrinsic to the ambiguity representation.

title: Segmenters have a measurable behavioral boundary between stuff and things that mismatches human intuition: stuff regions with countable texture elements (waves, clouds, foliage clumps) trigger thing-like fragmentation failures.
core_hypothesis: As stuff textures increase in element discreteness (from smooth water to distinct waves), segmentation behavior transitions from coherent regions to fragmented pseudo-instances at a measurable discreteness threshold, the threshold differs across models and from human judgments, and the transition zone concentrates a distinctive failure class (region shattering) invisible in standard per-class scores.

title: Segmenters misassign reflected and refracted content systematically by physical surface type: mirror content becomes objects, glass transmission merges with occluders, following a taxonomy predictable from surface optics rather than appearance.
core_hypothesis: Assignment errors (segmenting virtual content as real, merging transmitted with reflected layers) occur at rates and in directions determined by surface type and viewing geometry, forming a stable confusion structure across models, because training annotation conventions for each surface type are themselves systematically different and internally inconsistent.

title: Whether masks include attached shadows follows per-dataset annotation policy, and models trained on mixtures produce class-dependent shadow inclusion, creating an irreducible cross-dataset error floor that is pure convention conflict.
core_hypothesis: Model shadow-inclusion behavior is a learned mixture over training conventions, varying by class and context in ways traceable to source datasets, so a quantifiable fraction of cross-dataset boundary and region error is convention conflict that no model improvement can remove without a convention standard, and this fraction sets a floor on cross-dataset benchmark scores.

title: The same texture is classified as different categories depending on apparent scale, and segmenters lack scale anchoring: aerial and macro imagery elicits systematic class flips governed by patch-level scale ambiguity.
core_hypothesis: Per-region class posterior of segmenters is a function of apparent (pixel) scale with sharp class-flip boundaries, flips follow the training-set scale distribution per class rather than any scene-consistent scale inference, and injecting weak metric-scale cues (known object, GSD metadata encoding) removes a large share of flips, demonstrating the failure is missing scale anchoring rather than texture ambiguity.

title: Population-level smooth degradation under corruption is an aggregation artifact: per-instance failure is cliff-like, with each image having a sharp corruption threshold, which changes the correct mitigation strategy entirely.
core_hypothesis: For most corruption families, per-instance prediction-versus-severity trajectories are step functions (correct until an instance-specific threshold, then persistently wrong), the threshold distribution across instances generates the smooth population curve, and threshold location is predictable from instance-level features, so robustness should be framed as threshold-shifting rather than curve-flattening.

title: In-the-wild failure budgets are dominated by interactions between individually-handled factors (rain plus night, blur plus crowd), not by any single factor, making single-axis robustness benchmarks structurally unable to predict deployment failure.
core_hypothesis: A factorial decomposition of failure rates over nuisance-factor combinations will show pairwise and higher-order interaction terms contributing a larger share of total failure than main effects for realistic factor ranges, and models ranked identically on single-axis benchmarks will diverge widely on interaction cells, explaining why benchmark robustness fails to predict field reliability.

title: Robustness to a nuisance factor measured along one variation axis does not predict robustness along correlated real-world axes of the same factor: robustness is anisotropic, and benchmark axes are misaligned with natural variation.
core_hypothesis: For nuisance factors with multiple physical realizations (lighting: exposure versus spectrum versus direction; blur: motion versus defocus versus atmospheric), model robustness varies strongly across realizations, cross-realization correlation of per-model robustness is weak, and synthetic benchmark realizations sit systematically off the natural realization manifold, so benchmark-certified robustness fails to transfer to the field realization mix.

title: Vision models carry camera-model-specific failure biases: ISP pipelines (denoising, sharpening, tone mapping) leave fingerprints that shift model behavior, and a camera-fingerprint term explains failures currently attributed to content.
core_hypothesis: Per-device error rates on content-matched imagery differ significantly, the differences are attributable to ISP processing choices rather than optics (reprocessing RAW from one device through another device's ISP style transfers the error pattern), and adding a device-fingerprint covariate to failure models absorbs variance previously assigned to content categories.

title: Mined hard-case corpora cluster more by capture metadata (time, place, device, pipeline) than by visual content, so much of what failure mining calls content difficulty is recoverable provenance structure.
core_hypothesis: Clustering mined failure sets in metadata space will explain a substantial share of failure variance (higher than content-cluster explanations for a nontrivial fraction of clusters), metadata-matched control sampling will dissolve those clusters, and remediation targeted at the metadata stratum (pipeline fixes, acquisition changes) will outperform content-targeted retraining on them.

title: Failures concentrate in temporal transition regimes (rain onset, dusk, tunnel exits) rather than steady adverse states, because static datasets sample states, not transitions, leaving transition dynamics unlearned.
core_hypothesis: Failure rates during condition transitions exceed rates in either adjacent steady state at matched nominal difficulty, the excess is largest for transitions creating statistically novel mixtures rather than interpolations (wet-but-bright, headlights-in-daylight), and adding transition-sampled data reduces the excess more efficiently than adding more steady-state data.

title: Sensor-saturated pixels (highlight clipping, shadow crush) damage predictions superlinearly to their area because normalization and attention propagate clipping artifacts globally, making clipped fraction a strong hidden failure covariate.
core_hypothesis: Failure probability rises superlinearly with clipped-pixel fraction, the effect extends to predictions about unclipped regions (global leakage through normalization statistics and attention), and pre-inference clipping-aware treatment (masking, inpainting, statistics correction) recovers accuracy on unclipped content, demonstrating leakage rather than information loss as the mechanism.

title: Sim-to-real and real-to-sim failure is asymmetric per model, and the asymmetry direction reveals the model's feature reliance profile (texture-dependent versus geometry-dependent), providing a diagnostic no symmetric-gap analysis captures.
core_hypothesis: For matched content, per-model transfer degradation differs by direction (real-trained on sim versus sim-trained on real), texture-reliant models suffer more in the real-to-sim direction (missing natural texture statistics) while geometry-reliant models transfer more symmetrically, so the measured asymmetry index correlates with independent texture-bias measures and predicts which robustness interventions will help which model.

title: Most FM failures are linearly predictable from the model's own frozen features before the task head runs: failures are not surprises to the representation, only to the decision layer, enabling near-zero-cost failure prediction.
core_hypothesis: A linear probe on frozen FM features predicts per-input task failure substantially above chance across tasks and shifts, prediction transfers across task heads sharing the backbone (failure is encoded in the representation, not the head), and the probe's failures-it-cannot-predict form a small, structurally distinct residual (genuine ambiguity) rather than a random subset.

title: Per-instance loss-landscape sharpness at inference predicts which failures are fixable by fine-tuning and which persist: sharp failures resist repair and incur collateral damage, giving failure mining a repairability dimension.
core_hypothesis: A cheap per-instance sharpness proxy (loss sensitivity to small weight perturbations) computed at mining time predicts post-fine-tune repair success and collateral damage, sharp failures will be enriched in convention conflicts and label noise (where the target itself is inconsistent), and triaging mining outputs by repairability improves the retraining cost-benefit measurably.

title: Prediction inconsistency under imperceptible input jitter (sub-pixel shifts, quantization dither) marks failures better than confidence does, and the two signals disagree on a structured case subset where jitter is right and confidence is wrong.
core_hypothesis: A jitter-inconsistency score (prediction variance under a handful of imperceptible input perturbations) detects failures with higher precision-recall than max-confidence for boundary-proximal errors, the confidence-versus-jitter disagreement set is dominated by confidently-wrong shortcut cases (where both fail) and ambiguous cases (where jitter wins), and combining both signals approaches the practical ceiling of training-free failure detection.

title: Confidence-based hard-example mining recovers a biased sliver of the true failure distribution: it oversamples ambiguity failures, misses confident systematic failures, and thereby steers improvement loops away from the most dangerous errors.
core_hypothesis: Comparing exhaustively-labeled failure sets against confidence-mined subsets will show systematic composition bias (under-representation of high-confidence errors by large factors), retraining on confidence-mined data will improve diffident errors while leaving confident-error rates flat or worse, and mining by alternative signals (disagreement with cheap heuristics, jitter inconsistency, cross-model conflict) will recover complementary failure strata.

title: VLM verbalized confidence is generated from linguistic properties of its own draft answer rather than visual evidence: manipulating answer phrasing changes stated confidence while visual input stays fixed.
core_hypothesis: Verbalized confidence correlates more strongly with linguistic features of the emitted answer (fluency, specificity, answer length, hedging vocabulary availability) than with measured visual evidence strength, and interventions that alter the answer's linguistic frame (forcing specific formats, prefilling partial answers) shift stated confidence at fixed images, while visual-evidence interventions at fixed answer frames shift it far less than normative amounts.

title: Failure taxonomies produced by automated error-clustering tools are unstable under reruns, seeds, and embedding choices: the taxonomies describe the mining pipeline more than the model's failure structure.
core_hypothesis: Rerunning standard slice-discovery pipelines with perturbed seeds, embedding backbones, or clustering hyperparameters will produce taxonomies with low structural agreement (cluster matching scores near permutation baselines for many slices), the stable core will be small and coarse, and human teams shown taxonomies from different runs will make materially different remediation decisions, demonstrating that taxonomy instability propagates into engineering waste.

title: Fixing mined failures by fine-tuning damages a predictable collateral set of previously-correct cases, and the repair-damage exchange follows a measurable locality law in feature space, defining a conservation-like constraint on cheap fixes.
core_hypothesis: Post-repair regressions concentrate in feature-space neighborhoods of the repaired cases with damage probability decaying with representational distance, the decay profile is stable per architecture and fine-tuning method (defining a repair kernel), and total repair-minus-damage is approximately invariant across fine-tuning hyperparameters for fixed data, implying a budget that can be estimated before committing to a fix.

title: Which instances a model will fail on at convergence is largely determined early in training: learning-event signatures (forgetting counts, late first-learn epochs) forecast final failure sets long before training ends.
core_hypothesis: Per-instance training dynamics in the first fraction of training (forgetting events, first-learn time, loss oscillation) predict final-model failure membership substantially above chance, prediction transfers to held-out data via a dynamics-trained probe on input features, and the early-determined failure fraction is enriched in data-borne causes (label conflict, rare compositions) versus late-emerging failures that track optimization noise.

title: Frame-to-frame prediction flicker in video segmentation spikes seconds before catastrophic tracking losses: instability is a leading indicator with a usable warning horizon, not just a cosmetic artifact.
core_hypothesis: Catastrophic failure events in video segmentation and tracking are preceded by statistically elevated output instability (mask boundary churn, score oscillation) over a horizon of many frames, the precursor holds after controlling for scene difficulty dynamics, and thresholding the instability signal yields early warnings with operationally useful precision, while temporal smoothing (the standard remedy) destroys the warning signal without reducing catastrophe rates.

title: Motion-blur failure depends on blur direction relative to object contours and text orientation, not just magnitude: benchmarks using uniform-direction blur systematically mis-estimate real-world blur robustness.
core_hypothesis: At fixed blur magnitude, failure rates vary strongly with the angle between blur direction and dominant object contours (blur parallel to critical edges preserves them, perpendicular destroys them), so real-world blur robustness depends on the joint geometry of motion and content, and scalar-severity benchmarks misrank models whose directional profiles differ.

title: A large share of claimed temporal understanding in video models fails the shuffle test: predictions are invariant to frame order or time reversal, exposing single-frame shortcuts behind temporal benchmarks.
core_hypothesis: For current video models, a substantial fraction of correct answers on temporal-sounding tasks survives frame shuffling and time reversal, the surviving fraction varies strongly by task category (high for appearance-answerable, low for causal-order questions), and benchmark-level temporal capability scores shrink dramatically under order-sensitivity normalization, reordering model comparisons.

title: Tracker failures at occlusions are governed by a model-specific memory horizon: failure probability transitions sharply when occlusion duration exceeds a constant that is independent of object appearance, making occlusion risk computable from geometry alone.
core_hypothesis: Per-event tracking failure probability as a function of occlusion duration is sigmoid with a sharp model-specific midpoint (the memory horizon), the horizon is stable across object categories and appearance at matched re-detection difficulty, and horizon length measured on synthetic occlusions predicts real-world failure rates given deployment occlusion-duration distributions.

title: Video models fail on high-frame-rate and timelapse footage because the operative variable is motion magnitude per frame, not content: frame-rate mismatch is a hidden distribution shift misdiagnosed as content difficulty.
core_hypothesis: Video model accuracy is a function of inter-frame motion magnitude with a tuned optimum near web-typical values, degrading on both sides (too-small motion starves temporal signals, too-large motion breaks correspondence assumptions), so resampling deployment footage to web-typical motion-per-frame recovers accuracy without any model change, proving the failure is rate mismatch rather than content.

title: Deployed vision failures arrive in temporal bursts because consecutive inputs share failure-inducing conditions: per-image metrics understate operational risk, and the failure autocorrelation function is the missing deployment statistic.
core_hypothesis: Failure indicator time series from deployed streams exhibit strong positive autocorrelation over condition-persistence timescales, burst-adjusted risk metrics (probability of k consecutive failures) exceed IID predictions by orders of magnitude, and the autocorrelation function is predictable from environmental persistence statistics, enabling stream-level risk certification that per-image metrics cannot provide.

title: Failure mining only sees failures humans can adjudicate: models are never evaluated on inputs where human ground truth is unattainable, and the adjudication boundary silently shapes both training data and claimed capabilities.
core_hypothesis: Model behavior degrades or becomes pathological beyond the human adjudication boundary in ways detectable without full ground truth (via physical consistency checks, instrument cross-validation, or downstream outcome verification), and the excluded regime constitutes a substantial share of deployment inputs for real systems, so capability claims certified inside the boundary systematically overstate deployed reliability.

title: Benchmark-targeted training conserves failure mass rather than destroying it: as benchmarks saturate, failures migrate to input regions outside benchmark support, measurable as unchanged failure rates on independently sampled wild distributions.
core_hypothesis: For successive model generations optimized against saturated benchmarks, failure rates measured on continually refreshed, benchmark-disjoint wild samples decline far slower than benchmark gains imply, the divergence grows with benchmark age (a Goodhart drift law), and failure composition on wild samples shifts toward input types structurally absent from benchmark support, demonstrating migration rather than elimination.

title: Human-assigned failure categories (occlusion, blur, clutter) misidentify causal mechanisms: ablation-based causal attribution disagrees with human failure labels in a large fraction of cases, invalidating remediation plans built on human taxonomies.
core_hypothesis: For a substantial fraction of mined failures, counterfactual interventions (removing the occlusion, deblurring, decluttering via editing) do not flip the prediction, revealing the human-assigned cause was incidental, the true causes being invisible factors (context priors, convention conflicts, pipeline artifacts) that humans cannot see, so remediation targeted by human taxonomy fixes the wrong variable at scale.

title: A measurable share of benchmark failures are cases where ground truth is contested among annotators: model-truth disagreement and annotator-annotator disagreement overlap heavily, and separating them changes model rankings and failure-rate estimates.
core_hypothesis: Re-annotating benchmark samples with multiple independent annotators will show mined model failures strongly enriched in high-disagreement items, scoring only consensus items will change absolute failure rates substantially and reorder some model pairs, and the contested stratum will have distinct visual characteristics allowing cheap contestedness prediction for un-re-annotated benchmarks.

title: Specific systematic failures are fossils of training objectives, not data or architecture: loss-function swaps transplant characteristic failure signatures (boundary smoothing, dominant-mode collapse) across architectures and datasets.
core_hypothesis: Holding data and architecture fixed while swapping objectives (cross-entropy versus Dice versus boundary losses; softmax versus contrastive heads) will move characteristic failure signatures with the objective, the signatures will be recognizable across architectures trained with the same objective on different data, and a classifier can identify the training objective of a black-box model from its error structure alone, establishing objectives as dominant failure determinants.

title: Auto-labeling feedback loops amplify initial failure modes at a rate governed by the acceptance threshold: model-curated training data converts small biases into entrenched blind spots across iterations, with a measurable amplification law.
core_hypothesis: Iterated auto-label training amplifies precisely the confident systematic failures (which pass acceptance thresholds) while suppressing diffident errors, amplification rate per iteration is an increasing function of the acceptance threshold's confidence cutoff, and content strata initially failed confidently disappear progressively from effective training data, producing measurable coverage collapse invisible to aggregate metrics.

title: Published failure analyses over-represent photogenic, interpretable failure types while deployed error budgets are dominated by unglamorous causes (pipeline mismatches, threshold drift, metadata bugs): the literature's failure map is aesthetically curated.
core_hypothesis: Coding failure types reported in published analyses against failure-cause distributions from systematic deployment audits will reveal large, directional divergence: interpretable perceptual causes (adversarial patterns, unusual objects, occlusions) over-represented by large factors, and operational causes (preprocessing mismatch, calibration drift, version skew, metadata handling) under-represented, so research effort allocation tracks the aesthetic distribution rather than the harm distribution.
